title: Promote statusline and ccreport from macsetup to own repo
description:
The statusline and ccreport tooling currently lives in /Users/ove/git/macsetup/claude as flat PEP 723 scripts sharing a directory-level sys.path. Move it to this repo (/Users/ove/git/ccreport) as a proper src/ccreport package.

Source files: ccreport.py, statusline_command.py, cache_db.py, pricing.py, exchange.py, project_identity.py, get_claude_usage.py, banner_demo.py, benchmark_statusline_energy.py, statusline-command_x.sh, ccu.zsh, tests/ (11 files), docs/calculation-reference.md, CLAUDE.md (the AUDIT calculation reference), ruff.toml.

Decisions already made with the user:
- Layout: src/ccreport/ package. Modules become ccreport.pricing, ccreport.cache_db etc. Wrappers keep the sys.path + __pycache__ import trick, pointing at src/.
- History: fresh copy, no git-filter-repo. One commit on top of b9a0c6f.
- macsetup originals: LEAVE IN PLACE. Do not delete them and do not repoint mbp2022/settings.json, sbnorge/settings.json, zshrc/gadgets/claude_code/bin/ccreport, bin/ccu or dotlinks/dotlinks.toml. That cutover is a separate approved step.

Acceptance: just lint-all and just test pass in this repo; bin/ccreport and bin/statusline-command_x.sh run from a clean checkout; macsetup keeps working untouched.

Move cache, snapshot and config paths from macsetup/claude to ccreport
description:
The tooling still writes to paths named after its old home:
- src/ccreport/cache_db.py:29  DB_PATH = ~/.cache/macsetup/claude/cache.db  -> ~/.cache/ccreport/cache.db
- src/ccreport/cache_db.py:33  _DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_DIR = ~/.local/share/macsetup/claude/snapshots
- src/ccreport/project_identity.py:29  CONFIG_PATH = $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/macsetup/claude/ccreport.toml

The live DB is 163 MB of irreplaceable ccreport_records, so the move must not be a silent copy-on-next-run: an unmigrated machine would start a fresh empty DB and the old one would sit there unread. Add a 'ccreport migrate' command that moves the existing data to the new locations, is safe to run twice, and reports what it moved or found already done.
acceptance: ccreport migrate relocates an existing ~/.cache/macsetup/claude/cache.db; running it again is a no-op that says so; a machine with no old data exits cleanly; tests cover all three cases.

description: Move statusline-command_x.sh, ccu.zsh and the zshrc gadget's ccreport wrapper into bin/ in this repo and repoint their DIR resolution at src/. acceptance: just lint-all passes; bin/ccreport --help and a piped-stdin run of bin/statusline-command_x.sh both produce output.
notes:
Done. bin/ holds ccreport, statusline-command_x.sh and ccu.zsh.

Both bash wrappers dropped the PEP 723 machinery: this is a uv project now, not a set of inline-dependency scripts, so 'uv sync --script' plus 'uv python find --script' and the TMPDIR interpreter cache are all gone. They exec $REPO/.venv/bin/python directly, which is what the resolver was costing ~40ms per run to arrive at. The -c BOOT string that imports rather than runs the module — the thing that gets CPython to cache bytecode — is unchanged.

The status line falls back to python3 from PATH when there is no venv, because it and usage_api import nothing outside the stdlib. ccreport cannot: it needs orjson and rich, so it builds the venv once and errors if that fails.

pyproject.toml: orjson and rich are real dependencies now, plus a [project.scripts] ccreport entry point. macsetup's ruff.toml is folded into [tool.ruff] — line-length 110 and the full ignore list, not the scaffold's 88. just fmt no longer runs 'ruff format'; the wrapping in this tree is hand-chosen and a format pass rewrapped 1435 lines before that was caught.

pyright went from strict to standard: strict reported 5987 findings on this code, standard reported 71, and all 71 are fixed. 'just lint-all' passes.

description: Move statusline-command_x.sh, ccu.zsh and the zshrc gadget's ccreport wrapper into bin/ in this repo and repoint their DIR resolution at src/. pyproject.toml: orjson and rich are real dependencies now, plus a [project.scripts] ccreport entry point. macsetup's ruff.toml is folded into [tool.ruff] — line-length 110 and the full ignore list, not the scaffold's 88. just fmt no longer runs 'ruff format'; the wrapping in this tree is hand-chosen and a format pass rewrapped 1435 lines before that was caught.

pyright went from strict to standard: strict reported 5987 findings on this code, standard reported 71, and all 71 are fixed. 'just lint-all' passes.
closed_reason: Wrappers exec .venv/bin/python directly; ruff at 110 with no formatter, pyright at standard, both clean.

Source files: ccreport.py, statusline_command.py, cache_db.py, pricing.py, exchange.py, project_identity.py, get_claude_usage.py, banner_demo.py, benchmark_statusline_energy.py, statusline-command_x.sh, ccu.zsh, tests/ (11 files), docs/calculation-reference.md, CLAUDE.md (the AUDIT calculation reference), ruff.toml.

Decisions already made with the user:
- Layout: src/ccreport/ package. Modules become ccreport.pricing, ccreport.cache_db etc. Wrappers keep the sys.path + __pycache__ import trick, pointing at src/.
- History: fresh copy, no git-filter-repo. One commit on top of b9a0c6f.
- macsetup originals: LEAVE IN PLACE. Do not delete them and do not repoint mbp2022/settings.json, sbnorge/settings.json, zshrc/gadgets/claude_code/bin/ccreport, bin/ccu or dotlinks/dotlinks.toml. That cutover is a separate approved step.

Acceptance: just lint-all and just test pass in this repo; bin/ccreport and bin/statusline-command_x.sh run from a clean checkout; macsetup keeps working untouched.
closed_reason: All children done. Both tools run from their own repo; macsetup keeps only the pre-split copy under claude/orphaned_ccreport/.

title: Convert ccu.zsh to ccu.py
Convert ccu.zsh to ccu.py
acceptance: ccu and ccu --json produce the same output as the zsh version for the same usage row; jq is no longer required; pytest covers the rendering; bin/ccu.zsh is gone.
notes:
Done. src/ccreport/ccu.py replaces bin/ccu.zsh, which is deleted.

Output is unchanged — verified byte-for-byte against the zsh on the same usage row, at CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS of 3, 5 and 7, and on the argument-error path (both print the same usage line and exit 2).

jq is gone. So is the zsh: the repo has no shell beyond the three bin wrappers.

74 tests in tests/test_ccu.py cover the bar, the verbose countdown and its plurals, the reset line (today / tomorrow / further out / midnight / past / unparseable), the pace line and its five colour bands, the last-fetched header, section selection for optional quotas, main()'s exit codes, and fetch_usage against a stubbed subprocess. They pass under UTC, Europe/Oslo, America/New_York, Asia/Kolkata and Pacific/Chatham.

On the reuse question the issue asked me to check: the countdown and bar could not be shared. The status line renders a compact countdown ('1d2h') for a one-line bar and has no 50-cell meter at all; ccu renders words ('1 day and 2 hours'). Same delta, different products. What was genuinely shared is pace_days(), which now lives in pricing.py — both read CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS and two copies would drift. ccu also takes the week start from pricing.window_start_epoch() instead of the zsh's 'reset minus seven days'; they agree except when the reset has already passed, where the zsh went negative and printed nothing.

The fetch stays a subprocess. usage_api.main() owns a file lock, a cache TTL and a fetch-failure backoff on behalf of every reader, and reports by printing and exiting — calling it in-process would mean catching SystemExit and capturing stdout. It is also the seam the tests stub.

ccreport master: bd05733. The macsetup PATH forwarder needed its target changed from bin/ccu.zsh to bin/ccu; that edit is live and verified but left uncommitted.

Remove the macsetup legacy path auto-migration
description:
The cache, snapshot dir and config were relocated off their macsetup-era paths when this tooling left the macsetup repo. `cache_db.get_connection()` still stats the old cache dir on every open that finds no DB and calls `relocate_legacy_paths()`, and `ccreport migrate` exposes the same move on demand. One month after the move (created 2026-08-10) every machine has run it, so the code is dead weight carrying a legacy path constant, a CLI command and a test module.

Touchpoints:
- src/ccreport/cache_db.py:38-42 — the `_LEGACY_CACHE_DIR` / `_LEGACY_SNAPSHOT_DIR` constants and their comment
- src/ccreport/cache_db.py:465 `_move()` and :482 `relocate_legacy_paths()`
- src/ccreport/cache_db.py:521-523 — the auto-call in `get_connection()`
- src/ccreport/project_identity.py:32-33 — `LEGACY_CONFIG_PATH`
- src/ccreport/ccreport.py:1829 `cmd_migrate()` plus its subparser registration
- tests/test_migrate.py and the `LEGACY_CONFIG_PATH` monkeypatch in tests/conftest.py:35
- any mention in README.md / docs/

Before removing: confirm with the user that no machine of theirs still holds ~/.cache/macsetup/claude or ~/.config/macsetup/claude/ccreport.toml — removing the code strands that data rather than losing it, but it then needs a manual `mv`.
acceptance: No reference to macsetup paths remains in src/ or tests/; `ccreport migrate` is gone from the CLI and its help; `just lint-all` and `just test` pass; vulture_whitelist.py has no leftover entry for the removed symbols.

Bash-served full-line statusline cache, no Python on hits
description:
Serve a cache hit entirely from the bash wrapper, so a render costs no Python process at all.

Today every render execs python and goes through src/ccreport/statusline.py, even on the fast path: renders within FAST_TTL_S (15 s) already skip subprocess spawns and db reads by reusing the previous render's fetch results from a per-session temp file, and the wrapper bin/statusline-command_x.sh already skips the uv resolver. Prior measurement on an M-series machine, warm: ~110 ms before those two changes, ~25-30 ms after. What remains is interpreter startup and module import.

Proposal: cache the fully rendered line, with placeholders for the segments that must stay live. bin/statusline-command_x.sh serves that line on a hit and fills the placeholders itself — clock from $EPOCHSECONDS plus printf strftime, ctx% via jq from the stdin JSON. On a miss it falls through to Python as now. Estimated ~10 ms per hit.

Cost, which is why this is priority 3: a second formatting path in bash, and placeholder splicing that has to be kept in sync with the Python renderer whenever a segment's format changes. Only worth doing if ~25-30 ms still bothers us in practice. Requires bash 5 for $EPOCHSECONDS and printf %(fmt)T — /bin/bash is 3.2, so pin the shebang to the Homebrew bash — and jq on PATH.
acceptance:
- A cache hit renders with no python process spawned (verify with a process trace or a counter).
- Clock and ctx% are correct on every hit, not stale.
- Missing bash 5 or jq falls back to the Python renderer instead of erroring.
- Measured hit latency is reported in the issue before it moves to in_review.
- Tests under tests/ cover the placeholder contract between the Python renderer and the wrapper.

docs section 3 documents a PTY scrape that no longer exists
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:136-223 (section 3, Usage Percentage Parsing) describes usage_api.py finding the claude binary, spawning it in a PTY, stripping ANSI and regex-matching percentages and reset times, with a 15 s deadline. None of that exists: grep for pty/openpty across src/ returns nothing. usage_api.py does an HTTPS GET to https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with an OAuth token read from the macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json, and reset times arrive as resets_at fields.

Why it matters: usage_api.py's own AUDIT block points readers at this document as the authority. Anyone debugging a bad quota reading or reviewing how credentials are obtained follows a subsystem that was deleted in the macsetup to ccreport extraction.

Stale cross-references to the same section sit at docs/calculation-reference.md:362 and :390.
acceptance: Section 3 replaced with the HTTP path: the endpoint constant, both token sources, USAGE_API_TIMEOUT / RETRIES / RETRY_DELAY, _RETRYABLE_STATUS, _API_QUOTA_FIELDS, and the rule that an omitted quota field is a statement rather than a zero. The existing Fields Produced block is kept - it still matches. TOC and the two cross-references at :362 and :390 renumbered or repointed. No mention of pty, ANSI stripping or reset regexes remains in the file.

Frozen price table in the calculation reference is five model generations stale
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:55-70 carries a hand-copied price table headed 'Current Prices (as of LAST_CHECKED = 2026-02-22)'. pricing.py:116 reads LAST_CHECKED = 2026-07-24. The table ends at opus-4-6 and sonnet-4-6, so it lists none of opus-4-7, opus-4-8, opus-5, sonnet-5 (intro and standard), fable-5 or mythos-5. It also still shows the >200K premium rows that the 2026-03-13T18 pricing period removed.

Why it matters: this is money data. A reader reconciling a bill against the doc gets the wrong rate for every model in use today, plus a phantom long-context premium. AGENTS.md already states that all pricing data lives in pricing.py and only that file is updated when prices change - a second copy in the docs is a second thing to keep in step, and it has not been kept.

Copying the table again just restarts the clock. Replace it with a pointer.
acceptance: The date line and the price table are gone from docs/calculation-reference.md. In their place, one or two lines naming pricing.PRICING_HISTORY as the single source of truth and pricing.LAST_CHECKED as the freshness marker, with a note that prices are per-period and resolved by record timestamp. No model prices are duplicated anywhere outside pricing.py.

docs section 5.5 describes the pre-incremental session cache
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:443-455 says the session cost fingerprint is an md5 over the sorted (path, mtime_ns, size) tuples, and that a session is re-parsed whenever any file's mtime or size changes.

The code does something else. pricing._encode_session_state stores a versioned JSON blob: a version field, a per-file _FileCursor (mtime_ns, size, offset, tail) and dedup-key digests. pricing._decode_session_state:897 names the md5 shape explicitly as 'the pre-incremental md5 fingerprint' - the legacy form it still reads. A file that grew is resumed from its stored offset and tail digest, not re-parsed from the top.

Why it matters: the doc describes full invalidation where the code does incremental resume. A maintainer chasing a wrong session cost looks for the wrong failure mode, and the real one (a cursor that drifted from the file) is not documented at all.
acceptance: Section 5.5 rewritten around _SessionCostState and _SESSION_STATE_VERSION: what the blob holds, that a version mismatch costs one full reparse, that growth is resumed from offset plus the tail digest, and that the md5 form is legacy read-only. No claim that a changed file is re-parsed whole.

AGENTS.md warns about a deploy config file that does not exist
description:
AGENTS.md:145-147 says: 'git push itself can reach production - .deploy.remote.settings.toml sets git_push_after, so a deploy pushes as part of its run.'

There is no .deploy.remote.settings.toml in this repo and nothing configures a deploy. The clause is boilerplate carried over from another project.

Why it matters: it sits immediately after the real warning about --force, reset --hard and checkout -- ., which agents and humans do need. A false hazard next to a true one devalues the true one, and an agent reading it may refuse an ordinary push or invent a deploy step that does not exist.
acceptance: The .deploy.remote.settings.toml clause is deleted from AGENTS.md. The preceding sentence about git push --force, git reset --hard, git checkout -- . and branch deletion is kept unchanged. Nothing in the repo references .deploy.remote.settings.toml or git_push_after.

Sweep pre-extraction module names out of comments and docs
description:
About 20 sites name files that the macsetup to ccreport extraction renamed or deleted. A reader following any of these pointers finds nothing, and two of them are load-bearing instructions that therefore cannot be followed.

Old name -> current name:
  get_claude_usage.py      -> src/ccreport/usage_api.py
  statusline_command.py    -> src/ccreport/statusline.py
  test_get_claude_usage.py -> tests/test_usage_api.py
  claude/CLAUDE.md         -> docs/calculation-reference.md
  claude/pricing.py        -> src/ccreport/pricing.py
  claude/cache_db.py       -> src/ccreport/cache_db.py
  ccu.zsh                  -> src/ccreport/ccu.py
  claude/skills/           -> does not exist in this repo

Sites: pricing.py:4 and :7; statusline.py:67 and :690; ccreport.py:1982 and :2298; cache_db.py:1212, :1216, :1218, :2890; docs/calculation-reference.md:351, :548, :844, :1200-1204; tools/banner_demo.py:2 and :5; tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:5 and :17.

Two are load-bearing. pricing.py:7 is an AUDIT stanza telling a maintainer to update claude/CLAUDE.md after a pricing change - the four sibling modules (ccreport.py, statusline.py, usage_api.py, ccu.py) all name docs/calculation-reference.md, so this one is a rotted copy. cache_db.py:1212-1219 names get_claude_usage.FETCH_LOCK_MAX_HOLD_S and test_get_claude_usage.py TestFetchLockHoldBudget as what keeps two constants in step; the pointer to the coupling test is the comment's whole value.

Out of scope but worth knowing: tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:39 resolves HERE / statusline_command.py as a path, so just bench prints 'missing ...' and exits 1. That is a code bug, not a comment. Decide separately whether to point it at bin/statusline-command_x.sh.

Keep bin/ccu:2 ('Was ccu.zsh') - it is correct as history.

description:
131 macsetup-<id> references sit in comments, docstrings, migration headers and test class docstrings across 15 files (plus 7 more inside .dogcats/issues.jsonl, which is tracker data and stays).

Counts per file: cache_db.py 34, pricing.py 17, tests/test_cache_db.py 15, tests/test_pricing.py 12, tests/test_statusline.py 11, docs/calculation-reference.md 11, tests/test_ccreport.py 6, usage_api.py 6, ccreport.py 6, statusline.py 3, project_identity.py 3, tests/test_usage_cache.py 2, tests/test_usage_api.py 2, tests/test_migrate.py 1, tests/test_exchange.py 1.

Why they must go: macsetup is the repo this tooling left. This repo's tracker namespace is ccreport (.dogcats/config.toml), so a macsetup- id resolves to nothing even for a reader with tracker access. They are pure noise pointing at a system nobody here can query.

Most of them trail a complete sentence and can be deleted as a bare parenthetical - the surrounding prose already carries the rationale. Four sites are different: there the id IS the explanation, and deleting it leaves a sentence with no content. Recover the fact from the code and write it out instead:
  tests/test_cache_db.py:888  - 'the whole point of macsetup-qa61'
  tests/test_cache_db.py:907  - 'the whole safety argument for macsetup-45iv'
  tests/test_cache_db.py:1635 - 'as they stood before macsetup-45iv/3le2/4rpc'
  docs/calculation-reference.md:1191 - '(macsetup-3u9n decided it)'

Do not replace them with ccreport- ids. A comment that only resolves through a tracker is the defect; the fix is to state the fact in the comment.

description:
Measured numbers from one developer's machine are stated as permanent facts. Several have already rotted, and two contradict each other inside a single file.

Already wrong:
  cache_db.py:538 - 'runs 15 IF NOT EXISTS statements, six ALTERs raising and catching duplicate column'. The real counts are 16 CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS statements and 21 _ADDED_COLUMNS entries, and both grow with every schema addition. This is the cost that justifies the SCHEMA_VERSION gate, so it understates the whole argument.
  ccreport.py:448-452 - NokCtx._rate_memo says 'Half a million records span a few hundred days'. docs/calculation-reference.md:378-383 already carries an erratum saying this overstates the real corpus (~89K rows) by ~5x. A doc that annotates another file's docstring is two things to keep in step; fix the docstring and delete the erratum.
  pricing.py:526 says '96 of 88,801 cached rows on a real machine'; pricing.py:1166 says 'all but two of ~105k cached records on a real machine'. Two different census figures in one file.

Repeated censuses:
  'four rows carrying it are in this table permanently' at cache_db.py:2887, ccreport.py:2299, docs:1140 and tests/test_ccreport.py:2523 - one machine's rate_limit_snapshots count, in four places. Any further placeholder row makes all four wrong at once.
  docs:378-383 - '~89K rows across ~1,560 files and 90 distinct days (measured 2026-08-07)'.
  tests/test_statusline.py:220 - 'across all 23 .dogcats repos in ~/git'.
  statusline.py:841 says ~/.claude.json is 'a quarter of a megabyte'; tests/test_statusline.py:1042 says '~258 KB'. Same file, two spellings, both drift as the file grows.

Moving literal counts:
  pyproject.toml:42, :106, :191 - '215 lines here run over 88 and 32 over 100', '200+ sites and no formatter to add them', 'answers with 5987 findings'.
  bin/ccreport:12 - 'all 109 KB is tokenized'; bin/statusline-command_x.sh:22 - 'the whole 92 KB is tokenized'.

In every case the durable point survives without the number. The bytecode-cache rationale is 'the whole module', not its size; the dedup rationale is 'a small minority', not 96.

Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
description:
Six exported functions have behaviour that callers must handle and no docstring stating it. All are test-covered, so the behaviour is contract rather than accident.

1. pricing.compute_costs (pricing.py:1673) - the Cost buckets list documents 11 keys but the function returns 6 more (six_hour_project_cost through all_time_project_cost). It never states that session_window_cost is OMITTED rather than zeroed when no session reset is known - that omission is what statusline._merge_cost_data and usage_api._run_costs_only are built on, and zeroing it instead would carry the previous window's total across a rollover. The side effect (it caches the result via write_cost_summary) is also unstated.
2. ccreport.load_all_records (ccreport.py:802) - raises ValueError when use_rollups is passed together with since, until, project_filter or account_filter (ccreport.py:825-827). Undocumented.
3. cache_db.prefix_range (cache_db.py:1986) - raises ValueError on an empty prefix, with its own test. Undocumented. The reason is that an empty prefix would silently widen the range to the whole table.
4. ccreport.cmd_limits (ccreport.py:2540) - exits 1 when no samples exist and when the filters match nothing.
5. ccreport.cmd_adopt (ccreport.py:1917) - exits 1 when the capture log is empty.
6. cache_db.compute_extra_window_deltas (cache_db.py:1510) - never names the two keys it returns (extra_session_delta, extra_week_delta) or that None means no snapshot predates that window.

Smaller, same class: cache_db.usage_is_fresh, read_usage_cache and read_cost_summary (:1144, :1172, :3044) never say max_age is in seconds; usage_api.fetch_usage_api (:242) leaves its return contract at 'etc.' though the key set is _API_QUOTA_FIELDS and a test asserts the two are equal, and does not say HTTPError/URLError propagate once retries are exhausted.

Note: pyproject.toml disables D101/D102/D103/D107 deliberately so docstrings carry rationale rather than coverage. This issue is not about adding missing docstrings to internal helpers - it is about documented functions whose stated contract is incomplete.
acceptance: Each of the six carries the missing clause: compute_costs lists the project buckets, states the session_window_cost omission rule and the write_cost_summary side effect; load_all_records and prefix_range each have a Raises: ValueError line with the reason; cmd_limits and cmd_adopt each state when they exit 1; compute_extra_window_deltas names both keys and what None means. The three max_age docstrings say seconds. fetch_usage_api names _API_QUOTA_FIELDS instead of 'etc.' and states that HTTP and network errors propagate. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong
description:
This tree explains nearly every constant. These are the holes, each judged against its own neighbours in the same file.

1. cache_db.py:535 - PRAGMA cache_size = -2000. The comment explains only why the three pragmas sit outside the version gate, never that the negative sign is SQLite's KiB-versus-pages switch. 'Fixing' it to 2000 means 2000 pages, roughly 8 MB, per connection - on a path the status line opens every render.
2. ccreport.py:121 - CACHE_VERSION = 2 has no bump policy, while cache_db.SCHEMA_VERSION ('BUMP THIS on any change to...') and cache_db.CACHE_SCHEMA_SALT ('Bump this when...') both state theirs. It is also non-obviously not redundant with _script_hash(), which already hashes ccreport.py. So a maintainer either never bumps it or deletes it as dead weight.
3. The 10-minute usage TTL is spelled as a bare literal at four sites with nothing saying they must agree: usage_api.CACHE_MAX_AGE = 600, two max_age: int = 600 defaults in cache_db (:1172, :3044), and statusline.USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S = 600. That is a departure from this tree's rule of deriving key lists from one source and guarding drift with a test. Tuning one leaves the TTL check and the countdown the user reads describing different intervals.
4. statusline.py:125 - COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE = 900 is described as how long a cached compute_costs result stays usable, but nothing says it is what actually paces the costs-only refresh (via _fetch_usage's cost_summary is None branch), nor that the 300 s gap from USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S is deliberate. Aligning it to 600 changes how often a detached subprocess rescans the whole JSONL corpus.
5. cache_db.py:1203 - _BACKOFF_SCHEDULE = [45, 120, 240] names the unit and the index but gives no ceiling reasoning. Nothing says the last step must stay under the 600 s fetch interval; past that, one transient failure suppresses fetching indefinitely.
6. cache_db.py:43-44 - _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 10.0 and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT = 100 have no comment and are stranded under the legacy-paths block, so they read as belonging to it. The 10% is what decides whether real loss of unrebuildable orphan records gets reported.
7. cache_db.py:1503 - the 31-day snapshot prune. The comment restates the line and leaves 31 unexplained; the deltas this table feeds are the 5 h and 7 d windows, so 31 looks arbitrary. It is there because Extra usage is a monthly quota.
acceptance: Each of the seven carries a comment stating what breaks if the value moves, in this tree's existing style. title.new: Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong

description.new:
This tree explains nearly every constant. These are the holes, each judged against its own neighbours in the same file.

1. cache_db.py:535 - PRAGMA cache_size = -2000. The comment explains only why the three pragmas sit outside the version gate, never that the negative sign is SQLite's KiB-versus-pages switch. 'Fixing' it to 2000 means 2000 pages, roughly 8 MB, per connection - on a path the status line opens every render.
2. ccreport.py:121 - CACHE_VERSION = 2 has no bump policy, while cache_db.SCHEMA_VERSION ('BUMP THIS on any change to...') and cache_db.CACHE_SCHEMA_SALT ('Bump this when...') both state theirs. It is also non-obviously not redundant with _script_hash(), which already hashes ccreport.py. So a maintainer either never bumps it or deletes it as dead weight.
3. The 10-minute usage TTL is spelled as a bare literal at four sites with nothing saying they must agree: usage_api.CACHE_MAX_AGE = 600, two max_age: int = 600 defaults in cache_db (:1172, :3044), and statusline.USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S = 600. That is a departure from this tree's rule of deriving key lists from one source and guarding drift with a test. Tuning one leaves the TTL check and the countdown the user reads describing different intervals.
4. statusline.py:125 - COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE = 900 is described as how long a cached compute_costs result stays usable, but nothing says it is what actually paces the costs-only refresh (via _fetch_usage's cost_summary is None branch), nor that the 300 s gap from USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S is deliberate. Aligning it to 600 changes how often a detached subprocess rescans the whole JSONL corpus.
5. cache_db.py:1203 - _BACKOFF_SCHEDULE = [45, 120, 240] names the unit and the index but gives no ceiling reasoning. Nothing says the last step must stay under the 600 s fetch interval; past that, one transient failure suppresses fetching indefinitely.
6. cache_db.py:43-44 - _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 10.0 and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT = 100 have no comment and are stranded under the legacy-paths block, so they read as belonging to it. The 10% is what decides whether real loss of unrebuildable orphan records gets reported.
7. cache_db.py:1503 - the 31-day snapshot prune. The comment restates the line and leaves 31 unexplained; the deltas this table feeds are the 5 h and 7 d windows, so 31 looks arbitrary. It is there because Extra usage is a monthly quota.

exchange.py: walkback rationale, _max_date, and a comment naming a deleted function
description:
Three prose defects in one module, worth fixing in one pass.

1. exchange.py:21 - _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS = 10 is bare, though it is read in six places: it bounds the cached read horizon in _load_cached_rates, the start of every fetch span in _fetch_span, and the get_rate loop. Its three immediate neighbours (_MIN_PLAUSIBLE_RATE, _NO_OBSERVATION, _OBSERVATION_SETTLE_DAYS) each get a full paragraph. A maintainer trimming it to 5 on the reasoning that a long weekend is 3 days makes an Easter or Christmas holiday cluster unresolvable: get_rate returns (None, False) and those records drop out of the NOK column with no error.
2. exchange.py:300 - get_rate documents both return values and the walkback thoroughly but never mentions its third parameter _max_date. It is what decides the estimated flag, and precomputing it once is the whole reason a per-record caller can afford this function.
3. exchange.py:23 and tests/test_exchange.py:231 both explain themselves in terms of _find_missing_range, which no longer exists. The function is _fetch_span.

Also here, though it belongs to the restatement cleanup: exchange.py:316-319 repeats the estimated-at-the-trailing-edge rule that the docstring at :303-306 already states, inside a nine-line function.

  ccreport.py:553, 555 - one comment per line of a five-line function whose docstring already shows the transformation.
  cache_db.py:1563, 1569, 1577 (load_cost_cache); :1472, 1495, 1503; :2083, 2088; :1127 (restates _USAGE_COLS six lines above - keep the '# skip id column' below it, which explains the +1).
  statusline.py:257, 270, 313, 354, 1371, 1382 - six docstrings restating name plus return annotation; _extra_deltas and _ustr have docstrings longer than their bodies. Keep _collect_battery and _get_terminal_cols, which state a shape and an order.
  statusline.py:1252 - 'Remaining time until reset' over remain_s = int(reset_epoch - now).
  usage_api.py:153, 158, 287. Keep the neighbouring '# API returns cents; convert to dollars', which carries a unit.
  pricing.py:449, 1928, 1830.

Label-only dividers:

  ccu.py:338-340 - '# Entry point' in a file already ending in if __name__ == __main__.
  usage_api.py:300-302 - '# Main' over a 220-line grab-bag.

description:
None of these carries a wrong fact, so none needs deleting - each needs rewording.

1. statusline.py:1 - 'Claude Code status line - Python implementation for performance'. No checkable property; residue from the shell-to-Python rewrite. The real facts (renders on every frame, imports nothing outside the stdlib, defers cache_db into the functions that touch it) are stated further down and in AGENTS.md. Either shorten to the bare title or state the property.
2. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 - 'Seam Claude Code settings.json points at'. The tree calls this a wrapper everywhere else: README.md ('Point Claude Code settings.json at the wrapper'), bin/ccreport:2 ('A wrapper rather than a symlink'), AGENTS.md ('bin/ holds the wrappers'). 4. justfile:13 - '# run all formatters' above fmt-all: just fmt. There is exactly one, and AGENTS.md explicitly forbids adding a second ('Do not add ruff format to a recipe'). The plural invites the edit the project rules out.

description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:55-70 carries a hand-copied price table headed 'Current Prices (as of LAST_CHECKED = 2026-02-22)'. pricing.py:116 reads LAST_CHECKED = 2026-07-24. The table ends at opus-4-6 and sonnet-4-6, so it lists none of opus-4-7, opus-4-8, opus-5, sonnet-5 (intro and standard), fable-5 or mythos-5. It also still shows the >200K premium rows that the 2026-03-13T18 pricing period removed.

Why it matters: this is money data. A reader reconciling a bill against the doc gets the wrong rate for every model in use today, plus a phantom long-context premium. AGENTS.md already states that all pricing data lives in pricing.py and only that file is updated when prices change - a second copy in the docs is a second thing to keep in step, and it has not been kept.

Copying the table again just restarts the clock. Replace it with a pointer.
acceptance: The date line and the price table are gone from docs/calculation-reference.md. In their place, one or two lines naming pricing.PRICING_HISTORY as the single source of truth and pricing.LAST_CHECKED as the freshness marker, with a note that prices are per-period and resolved by record timestamp. No model prices are duplicated anywhere outside pricing.py.

docs section 5.5 describes the pre-incremental session cache
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:443-455 says the session cost fingerprint is an md5 over the sorted (path, mtime_ns, size) tuples, and that a session is re-parsed whenever any file's mtime or size changes.

The code does something else. pricing._encode_session_state stores a versioned JSON blob: a version field, a per-file _FileCursor (mtime_ns, size, offset, tail) and dedup-key digests. pricing._decode_session_state:897 names the md5 shape explicitly as 'the pre-incremental md5 fingerprint' - the legacy form it still reads. A file that grew is resumed from its stored offset and tail digest, not re-parsed from the top.

Why it matters: the doc describes full invalidation where the code does incremental resume. A maintainer chasing a wrong session cost looks for the wrong failure mode, and the real one (a cursor that drifted from the file) is not documented at all.
acceptance: Section 5.5 rewritten around _SessionCostState and _SESSION_STATE_VERSION: what the blob holds, that a version mismatch costs one full reparse, that growth is resumed from offset plus the tail digest, and that the md5 form is legacy read-only. No claim that a changed file is re-parsed whole.

description:
AGENTS.md:145-147 says: 'git push itself can reach production - .deploy.remote.settings.toml sets git_push_after, so a deploy pushes as part of its run.'

There is no .deploy.remote.settings.toml in this repo and nothing configures a deploy. The clause is boilerplate carried over from another project.

Why it matters: it sits immediately after the real warning about --force, reset --hard and checkout -- ., which agents and humans do need. A false hazard next to a true one devalues the true one, and an agent reading it may refuse an ordinary push or invent a deploy step that does not exist.
acceptance: The .deploy.remote.settings.toml clause is deleted from AGENTS.md. The preceding sentence about git push --force, git reset --hard, git checkout -- . and branch deletion is kept unchanged. Nothing in the repo references .deploy.remote.settings.toml or git_push_after.

description:
131 macsetup-<id> references sit in comments, docstrings, migration headers and test class docstrings across 15 files (plus 7 more inside .dogcats/issues.jsonl, which is tracker data and stays).

description:
Six independent drift points in the reference doc, separate from the section 3, section 5.5 and price-table issues:

1. :840-842 documents CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_WRAP=1 as a line separator between the three output sections. grep for WRAP across src/, bin/ and tests/ finds only this doc mention. A user sets it and nothing happens.
2. :357-374 section 5.1 lists 13 tables; cache_db._SCHEMA_SQL creates 16. Missing: ccreport_rollups, ccreport_orphan_costs, project_scopes. project_scopes is discussed in the prose of 5.6 yet absent from the inventory above it, and AGENTS.md treats ccreport_rollups as central to a bare ccreport run.
3. :227 says compute_costs produces ten cost buckets; the table two lines below lists 16, and the set is derived from pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS so it moves whenever a window is added.
4. :885-890 gives the weekly pace formula as elapsed_s * 100 / (7 * 86400). ccu.pace_line:226-242 divides by pricing.pace_days(), which reads CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS (README documents it), and prints a '(pace: Nd)' fragment the doc omits.
5. :864 shows the progress bar as '#' characters in green and dark gray. ccu.py:209-210 draws the block glyphs at BAR_WIDTH = 50.
6. :9 TOC anchor #5-caching-strategy--cache-formats no longer matches the heading at :349; :721 cross-references 'the cache-stats file from 5.3' when cache stats is 5.4 and is a table, not a file.
acceptance: The WRAP section is deleted (or repointed at a real env var if one exists). Section 5.1 lists all 16 tables and states that it is the inventory of cache_db._SCHEMA_SQL. The bucket count at :227 is replaced with a derivation from pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS rather than a literal. The pace formula uses pace_days() and shows the (pace: Nd) fragment, cross-referencing the README env var. The bar sample matches ccu.py's glyphs and cites BAR_WIDTH. The TOC anchor and the 5.3 cross-reference resolve.

title: Remaining drift in docs/calculation-reference.md
statusline.py env-var table is wrong in three places
description:
README.md points at the statusline.py module docstring as the full list of env vars with defaults, so this table is the user-facing reference.

Also at :690, the _fetch_usage docstring summary reads 'env var -> cache bypass -> detached get_claude_usage.py'. There is no cache-bypass step: the path is env var, then one read of the cached usage row, return it if fresh, otherwise spawn a detached refresh and return the stale row anyway.

title: Sweep pre-extraction module names out of comments and docs
Replace rot-prone literal counts and one-machine anecdotes
description:
Measured numbers from one developer's machine are stated as permanent facts. Several have already rotted, and two contradict each other inside a single file.

Already wrong:
  cache_db.py:538 - 'runs 15 IF NOT EXISTS statements, six ALTERs raising and catching duplicate column'. The real counts are 16 CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS statements and 21 _ADDED_COLUMNS entries, and both grow with every schema addition. This is the cost that justifies the SCHEMA_VERSION gate, so it understates the whole argument.
  ccreport.py:448-452 - NokCtx._rate_memo says 'Half a million records span a few hundred days'. docs/calculation-reference.md:378-383 already carries an erratum saying this overstates the real corpus (~89K rows) by ~5x. A doc that annotates another file's docstring is two things to keep in step; fix the docstring and delete the erratum.
  pricing.py:526 says '96 of 88,801 cached rows on a real machine'; pricing.py:1166 says 'all but two of ~105k cached records on a real machine'. Two different census figures in one file.

Repeated censuses:
  'four rows carrying it are in this table permanently' at cache_db.py:2887, ccreport.py:2299, docs:1140 and tests/test_ccreport.py:2523 - one machine's rate_limit_snapshots count, in four places. Any further placeholder row makes all four wrong at once.
  docs:378-383 - '~89K rows across ~1,560 files and 90 distinct days (measured 2026-08-07)'.
  tests/test_statusline.py:220 - 'across all 23 .dogcats repos in ~/git'.
  statusline.py:841 says ~/.claude.json is 'a quarter of a megabyte'; tests/test_statusline.py:1042 says '~258 KB'. Same file, two spellings, both drift as the file grows.

Moving literal counts:
  pyproject.toml:42, :106, :191 - '215 lines here run over 88 and 32 over 100', '200+ sites and no formatter to add them', 'answers with 5987 findings'.
  bin/ccreport:12 - 'all 109 KB is tokenized'; bin/statusline-command_x.sh:22 - 'the whole 92 KB is tokenized'.

In every case the durable point survives without the number. The bytecode-cache rationale is 'the whole module', not its size; the dedup rationale is 'a small minority', not 96.
acceptance: No comment or docstring in src/, tests/, tools/, bin/, docs/ or pyproject.toml states a row count, file count, byte size, finding count or line count measured from one machine. cache_db.py:538 describes the bootstrap shape rather than counting it. The NokCtx._rate_memo docstring carries no figure and the docs erratum paragraph is deleted. The four 'four rows' sites say that rows written before the lookahead check carry the placeholder. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Replace rot-prone literal counts and one-machine anecdotes
Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
description:
Six exported functions have behaviour that callers must handle and no docstring stating it. All are test-covered, so the behaviour is contract rather than accident.

1. pricing.compute_costs (pricing.py:1673) - the Cost buckets list documents 11 keys but the function returns 6 more (six_hour_project_cost through all_time_project_cost). It never states that session_window_cost is OMITTED rather than zeroed when no session reset is known - that omission is what statusline._merge_cost_data and usage_api._run_costs_only are built on, and zeroing it instead would carry the previous window's total across a rollover. The side effect (it caches the result via write_cost_summary) is also unstated.
2. ccreport.load_all_records (ccreport.py:802) - raises ValueError when use_rollups is passed together with since, until, project_filter or account_filter (ccreport.py:825-827). Undocumented.
3. cache_db.prefix_range (cache_db.py:1986) - raises ValueError on an empty prefix, with its own test. Undocumented. The reason is that an empty prefix would silently widen the range to the whole table.
4. ccreport.cmd_limits (ccreport.py:2540) - exits 1 when no samples exist and when the filters match nothing.
5. ccreport.cmd_adopt (ccreport.py:1917) - exits 1 when the capture log is empty.
6. cache_db.compute_extra_window_deltas (cache_db.py:1510) - never names the two keys it returns (extra_session_delta, extra_week_delta) or that None means no snapshot predates that window.

Smaller, same class: cache_db.usage_is_fresh, read_usage_cache and read_cost_summary (:1144, :1172, :3044) never say max_age is in seconds; usage_api.fetch_usage_api (:242) leaves its return contract at 'etc.' though the key set is _API_QUOTA_FIELDS and a test asserts the two are equal, and does not say HTTPError/URLError propagate once retries are exhausted.

Note: pyproject.toml disables D101/D102/D103/D107 deliberately so docstrings carry rationale rather than coverage. This issue is not about adding missing docstrings to internal helpers - it is about documented functions whose stated contract is incomplete.
acceptance: Each of the six carries the missing clause: compute_costs lists the project buckets, states the session_window_cost omission rule and the write_cost_summary side effect; load_all_records and prefix_range each have a Raises: ValueError line with the reason; cmd_limits and cmd_adopt each state when they exit 1; compute_extra_window_deltas names both keys and what None means. The three max_age docstrings say seconds. fetch_usage_api names _API_QUOTA_FIELDS instead of 'etc.' and states that HTTP and network errors propagate. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong
description:
This tree explains nearly every constant. These are the holes, each judged against its own neighbours in the same file.

1. cache_db.py:535 - PRAGMA cache_size = -2000. The comment explains only why the three pragmas sit outside the version gate, never that the negative sign is SQLite's KiB-versus-pages switch. 'Fixing' it to 2000 means 2000 pages, roughly 8 MB, per connection - on a path the status line opens every render.
2. ccreport.py:121 - CACHE_VERSION = 2 has no bump policy, while cache_db.SCHEMA_VERSION ('BUMP THIS on any change to...') and cache_db.CACHE_SCHEMA_SALT ('Bump this when...') both state theirs. It is also non-obviously not redundant with _script_hash(), which already hashes ccreport.py. So a maintainer either never bumps it or deletes it as dead weight.
3. The 10-minute usage TTL is spelled as a bare literal at four sites with nothing saying they must agree: usage_api.CACHE_MAX_AGE = 600, two max_age: int = 600 defaults in cache_db (:1172, :3044), and statusline.USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S = 600. That is a departure from this tree's rule of deriving key lists from one source and guarding drift with a test. Tuning one leaves the TTL check and the countdown the user reads describing different intervals.
4. statusline.py:125 - COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE = 900 is described as how long a cached compute_costs result stays usable, but nothing says it is what actually paces the costs-only refresh (via _fetch_usage's cost_summary is None branch), nor that the 300 s gap from USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S is deliberate. Aligning it to 600 changes how often a detached subprocess rescans the whole JSONL corpus.
5. cache_db.py:1203 - _BACKOFF_SCHEDULE = [45, 120, 240] names the unit and the index but gives no ceiling reasoning. Nothing says the last step must stay under the 600 s fetch interval; past that, one transient failure suppresses fetching indefinitely.
6. cache_db.py:43-44 - _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 10.0 and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT = 100 have no comment and are stranded under the legacy-paths block, so they read as belonging to it. The 10% is what decides whether real loss of unrebuildable orphan records gets reported.
7. cache_db.py:1503 - the 31-day snapshot prune. The comment restates the line and leaves 31 unexplained; the deltas this table feeds are the 5 h and 7 d windows, so 31 looks arbitrary. It is there because Extra usage is a monthly quota.
acceptance: Each of the seven carries a comment stating what breaks if the value moves, in this tree's existing style. The TTL item names one authority and says why the other three are spelled out rather than imported. _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT are moved out from under the legacy-paths block. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong
exchange.py: walkback rationale, _max_date, and a comment naming a deleted function
description:
Three prose defects in one module, worth fixing in one pass.

1. exchange.py:21 - _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS = 10 is bare, though it is read in six places: it bounds the cached read horizon in _load_cached_rates, the start of every fetch span in _fetch_span, and the get_rate loop. Its three immediate neighbours (_MIN_PLAUSIBLE_RATE, _NO_OBSERVATION, _OBSERVATION_SETTLE_DAYS) each get a full paragraph. A maintainer trimming it to 5 on the reasoning that a long weekend is 3 days makes an Easter or Christmas holiday cluster unresolvable: get_rate returns (None, False) and those records drop out of the NOK column with no error.
2. exchange.py:300 - get_rate documents both return values and the walkback thoroughly but never mentions its third parameter _max_date. It is what decides the estimated flag, and precomputing it once is the whole reason a per-record caller can afford this function.
3. exchange.py:23 and tests/test_exchange.py:231 both explain themselves in terms of _find_missing_range, which no longer exists. The function is _fetch_span.

Also here, though it belongs to the restatement cleanup: exchange.py:316-319 repeats the estimated-at-the-trailing-edge rule that the docstring at :303-306 already states, inside a nine-line function.
acceptance: _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS carries a comment naming what it bounds and what silently breaks if it is lowered. get_rate's docstring documents _max_date and why it is passed in. grep for _find_missing_range across the repo returns nothing. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: exchange.py: walkback rationale, _max_date, and a comment naming a deleted function
One rationale is re-argued at every observer instead of stated once
description:
Three constraints are each told in full at many sites. Every individual copy carries a real fact - this is verbosity, not error, so the fix is to keep the canonical statement where the constraint is enforced and leave the observers with a bare pointer. Do not delete the rationale.

Rate-limit reset drift, the 9999999999 placeholder, and 'never pruned' - told in full at cache_db.py:304-328 (the CREATE TABLE), RL_MAX_LOOKAHEAD_S (:2884-2892), rl_window_key (:2896-2921), record_rate_limit_snapshots (:2939+), load_rate_limit_snapshots (:2997+), statusline._rl_sample (:875+), ccreport._implausible_reset (:2295+), ccreport._window_instances (:2127+), AGENTS.md:98-114 and docs section 9.6. The same drift observation appears verbatim in three of them.
2. Account capture and attribution - cache_db's CREATE TABLE, record_account_event, AGENTS.md:80-97, statusline._capture_account, and docs 9.1 through 9.5.
3. The snapshot deferral - cache_db.py:805-828, _daily_snapshot_deferred, _refresh_env, statusline.main, ccreport.main and two test class docstrings.

Individual over-length sites worth trimming in the same pass:

  pricing.py:1286-1310 - a 25-line docstring for two facts; the caching story is already docs 5.6.
  statusline.py:833-851 - trim the first two paragraphs, replace the third with one best-effort line.

title: One rationale is re-argued at every observer instead of stated once
Delete comments that restate the line below them, and label-only dividers
description:
About 50 sites where the prose adds nothing the code does not already say. pyproject.toml disables D103 precisely so docstrings can carry rationale rather than coverage, so these run against the project's own stated norm and bury the real comments around them.

Restatement, one comment per statement:
  ccreport.py:2763 - 'No subcommand: show daily + monthly summary'. The else branch already says no subcommand, and the block calls report_daily, report_monthly, report_project, report_session and conditionally report_account - the comment names two of five.
  ccreport.py:1427, 1466, 1534, 1626, 492, 562, 1167, 1177, 1188, 1300, 1336 - eleven docstrings that are the function name with spaces added. Keep fmt_tokens, fmt_cost, _fmt_cache_read and short_model, which state a threshold or show sample output.
  ccreport.py:553, 555 - one comment per line of a five-line function whose docstring already shows the transformation.
  cache_db.py:1563, 1569, 1577 (load_cost_cache); :1472, 1495, 1503; :2083, 2088; :1127 (restates _USAGE_COLS six lines above - keep the '# skip id column' below it, which explains the +1).
  statusline.py:257, 270, 313, 354, 1371, 1382 - six docstrings restating name plus return annotation; _extra_deltas and _ustr have docstrings longer than their bodies. Keep _collect_battery and _get_terminal_cols, which state a shape and an order.
  statusline.py:1252 - 'Remaining time until reset' over remain_s = int(reset_epoch - now).
  usage_api.py:153, 158, 287. Keep the neighbouring '# API returns cents; convert to dollars', which carries a unit.
  pricing.py:449, 1928, 1830.
  exchange.py:316-319 - a verbatim repeat of the docstring twelve lines above.

Label-only dividers:
  statusline.py:115-117 - two labels for the same block, two lines apart; delete the first.
  statusline.py:1753 - '# --- Main ---' over ~600 lines holding the cost merge, input parsing, layout, the fetch cache and main(). Delete or name what it holds.
  ccu.py:338-340 - '# Entry point' in a file already ending in if __name__ == __main__.
  usage_api.py:300-302 - '# Main' over a 220-line grab-bag.
  usage_api.py:66 - 'HTTP status codes worth retrying' over _RETRYABLE_STATUS.
  pricing.py:1807 and :1822 - dividers restating the docstring and the call directly beneath them.
  tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:129, 133, 156 - phase dividers duplicating the log() call on the next line.
  tests/test_pricing.py - 23 divider blocks (46 comment lines) in a 2,757-line module; twelve are pure label restatement of the class immediately below. The divider count is the file asking to be split into modules; if the split is deferred, delete those twelve.

Deliberately protected - do not touch: cache_db.py's 15 section dividers (several carry load-bearing prose), statusline.py's per-segment dividers which navigate a 2,376-line file, tests/test_exchange.py's five dividers grouping module-level functions, and the aligned trailing comments on schema columns and constants, which carry units, sentinel meanings and NULL semantics.

title: Delete comments that restate the line below them, and label-only dividers
Four prose nits that state no checkable property
description:
None of these carries a wrong fact, so none needs deleting - each needs rewording.

1. statusline.py:1 - 'Claude Code status line - Python implementation for performance'. No checkable property; residue from the shell-to-Python rewrite. The real facts (renders on every frame, imports nothing outside the stdlib, defers cache_db into the functions that touch it) are stated further down and in AGENTS.md. Either shorten to the bare title or state the property.
2. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 - 'Seam Claude Code settings.json points at'. The tree calls this a wrapper everywhere else: README.md ('Point Claude Code settings.json at the wrapper'), bin/ccreport:2 ('A wrapper rather than a symlink'), AGENTS.md ('bin/ holds the wrappers'). One file renames the thing. Note that ccu.py:9's use of 'seam' is precise - it names the boundary the tests stub - and should stay.
3. exchange.py:3-4 - 'Fetches from the Norges Bank SDMX-JSON API, caches in SQLite, and provides rate lookups with automatic fallback for weekends and holidays'. The third item restates the first two; 'provides rate lookups' dodges a plain verb and 'automatic' adds nothing a caller can act on.
4. justfile:13 - '# run all formatters' above fmt-all: just fmt. There is exactly one, and AGENTS.md explicitly forbids adding a second ('Do not add ruff format to a recipe'). The plural invites the edit the project rules out.
acceptance: Each of the four is reworded. statusline.py:1 either states a property or is a bare title. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 says wrapper; ccu.py:9 is untouched. exchange.py's module docstring names what get_rate does in plain verbs. justfile:13 says there is deliberately one formatter.

title: Four prose nits that state no checkable property
docs section 3 documents a PTY scrape that no longer exists
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:136-223 (section 3, Usage Percentage Parsing) describes usage_api.py finding the claude binary, spawning it in a PTY, stripping ANSI and regex-matching percentages and reset times, with a 15 s deadline. None of that exists: grep for pty/openpty across src/ returns nothing. usage_api.py does an HTTPS GET to https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with an OAuth token read from the macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json, and reset times arrive as resets_at fields.

Why it matters: usage_api.py's own AUDIT block points readers at this document as the authority. Anyone debugging a bad quota reading or reviewing how credentials are obtained follows a subsystem that was deleted in the macsetup to ccreport extraction.

Stale cross-references to the same section sit at docs/calculation-reference.md:362 and :390.
acceptance: Section 3 replaced with the HTTP path: the endpoint constant, both token sources, USAGE_API_TIMEOUT / RETRIES / RETRY_DELAY, _RETRYABLE_STATUS, _API_QUOTA_FIELDS, and the rule that an omitted quota field is a statement rather than a zero. The existing Fields Produced block is kept - it still matches. TOC and the two cross-references at :362 and :390 renumbered or repointed. No mention of pty, ANSI stripping or reset regexes remains in the file.

title: docs section 3 documents a PTY scrape that no longer exists
Frozen price table in the calculation reference is five model generations stale
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:55-70 carries a hand-copied price table headed 'Current Prices (as of LAST_CHECKED = 2026-02-22)'. pricing.py:116 reads LAST_CHECKED = 2026-07-24. The table ends at opus-4-6 and sonnet-4-6, so it lists none of opus-4-7, opus-4-8, opus-5, sonnet-5 (intro and standard), fable-5 or mythos-5. It also still shows the >200K premium rows that the 2026-03-13T18 pricing period removed.

Why it matters: this is money data. A reader reconciling a bill against the doc gets the wrong rate for every model in use today, plus a phantom long-context premium. AGENTS.md already states that all pricing data lives in pricing.py and only that file is updated when prices change - a second copy in the docs is a second thing to keep in step, and it has not been kept.

Copying the table again just restarts the clock. Replace it with a pointer.
acceptance: The date line and the price table are gone from docs/calculation-reference.md. In their place, one or two lines naming pricing.PRICING_HISTORY as the single source of truth and pricing.LAST_CHECKED as the freshness marker, with a note that prices are per-period and resolved by record timestamp. No model prices are duplicated anywhere outside pricing.py.

title: Frozen price table in the calculation reference is five model generations stale
docs section 5.5 describes the pre-incremental session cache
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:443-455 says the session cost fingerprint is an md5 over the sorted (path, mtime_ns, size) tuples, and that a session is re-parsed whenever any file's mtime or size changes.

The code does something else. pricing._encode_session_state stores a versioned JSON blob: a version field, a per-file _FileCursor (mtime_ns, size, offset, tail) and dedup-key digests. pricing._decode_session_state:897 names the md5 shape explicitly as 'the pre-incremental md5 fingerprint' - the legacy form it still reads. A file that grew is resumed from its stored offset and tail digest, not re-parsed from the top.

Why it matters: the doc describes full invalidation where the code does incremental resume. A maintainer chasing a wrong session cost looks for the wrong failure mode, and the real one (a cursor that drifted from the file) is not documented at all.
acceptance: Section 5.5 rewritten around _SessionCostState and _SESSION_STATE_VERSION: what the blob holds, that a version mismatch costs one full reparse, that growth is resumed from offset plus the tail digest, and that the md5 form is legacy read-only. No claim that a changed file is re-parsed whole.

title: docs section 5.5 describes the pre-incremental session cache
AGENTS.md warns about a deploy config file that does not exist
description:
AGENTS.md:145-147 says: 'git push itself can reach production - .deploy.remote.settings.toml sets git_push_after, so a deploy pushes as part of its run.'

There is no .deploy.remote.settings.toml in this repo and nothing configures a deploy. The clause is boilerplate carried over from another project.

Why it matters: it sits immediately after the real warning about --force, reset --hard and checkout -- ., which agents and humans do need. A false hazard next to a true one devalues the true one, and an agent reading it may refuse an ordinary push or invent a deploy step that does not exist.
acceptance: The .deploy.remote.settings.toml clause is deleted from AGENTS.md. The preceding sentence about git push --force, git reset --hard, git checkout -- . and branch deletion is kept unchanged. Nothing in the repo references .deploy.remote.settings.toml or git_push_after.

title: AGENTS.md warns about a deploy config file that does not exist
Purge macsetup- ticket ids from every comment, docstring and doc
description:
131 macsetup-<id> references sit in comments, docstrings, migration headers and test class docstrings across 15 files (plus 7 more inside .dogcats/issues.jsonl, which is tracker data and stays).

Counts per file: cache_db.py 34, pricing.py 17, tests/test_cache_db.py 15, tests/test_pricing.py 12, tests/test_statusline.py 11, docs/calculation-reference.md 11, tests/test_ccreport.py 6, usage_api.py 6, ccreport.py 6, statusline.py 3, project_identity.py 3, tests/test_usage_cache.py 2, tests/test_usage_api.py 2, tests/test_migrate.py 1, tests/test_exchange.py 1.

Why they must go: macsetup is the repo this tooling left. This repo's tracker namespace is ccreport (.dogcats/config.toml), so a macsetup- id resolves to nothing even for a reader with tracker access. They are pure noise pointing at a system nobody here can query.

Most of them trail a complete sentence and can be deleted as a bare parenthetical - the surrounding prose already carries the rationale. Four sites are different: there the id IS the explanation, and deleting it leaves a sentence with no content. Recover the fact from the code and write it out instead:
  tests/test_cache_db.py:888  - 'the whole point of macsetup-qa61'
  tests/test_cache_db.py:907  - 'the whole safety argument for macsetup-45iv'
  tests/test_cache_db.py:1635 - 'as they stood before macsetup-45iv/3le2/4rpc'
  docs/calculation-reference.md:1191 - '(macsetup-3u9n decided it)'

Do not replace them with ccreport- ids. A comment that only resolves through a tracker is the defect; the fix is to state the fact in the comment.
acceptance: grep -rn 'macsetup-' across src/, tests/, tools/, docs/, bin/ and the markdown files at the root returns nothing. The four sites above each carry a written-out fact in place of the id. Every other deletion leaves a grammatical sentence that still states its rationale. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Purge macsetup- ticket ids from every comment, docstring and doc
Remaining drift in docs/calculation-reference.md
description:
Six independent drift points in the reference doc, separate from the section 3, section 5.5 and price-table issues:

1. :840-842 documents CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_WRAP=1 as a line separator between the three output sections. grep for WRAP across src/, bin/ and tests/ finds only this doc mention. A user sets it and nothing happens.
2. :357-374 section 5.1 lists 13 tables; cache_db._SCHEMA_SQL creates 16. Missing: ccreport_rollups, ccreport_orphan_costs, project_scopes. project_scopes is discussed in the prose of 5.6 yet absent from the inventory above it, and AGENTS.md treats ccreport_rollups as central to a bare ccreport run.
3. :227 says compute_costs produces ten cost buckets; the table two lines below lists 16, and the set is derived from pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS so it moves whenever a window is added.
4. :885-890 gives the weekly pace formula as elapsed_s * 100 / (7 * 86400). ccu.pace_line:226-242 divides by pricing.pace_days(), which reads CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS (README documents it), and prints a '(pace: Nd)' fragment the doc omits.
5. :864 shows the progress bar as '#' characters in green and dark gray. ccu.py:209-210 draws the block glyphs at BAR_WIDTH = 50.
6. :9 TOC anchor #5-caching-strategy--cache-formats no longer matches the heading at :349; :721 cross-references 'the cache-stats file from 5.3' when cache stats is 5.4 and is a table, not a file.
acceptance: The WRAP section is deleted (or repointed at a real env var if one exists). Section 5.1 lists all 16 tables and states that it is the inventory of cache_db._SCHEMA_SQL. The bucket count at :227 is replaced with a derivation from pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS rather than a literal. The pace formula uses pace_days() and shows the (pace: Nd) fragment, cross-referencing the README env var. The bar sample matches ccu.py's glyphs and cites BAR_WIDTH. The TOC anchor and the 5.3 cross-reference resolve.

title: Remaining drift in docs/calculation-reference.md
statusline.py env-var table is wrong in three places
description:
README.md points at the statusline.py module docstring as the full list of env vars with defaults, so this table is the user-facing reference.

1. :47 documents CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_WEEKLY_PACE with the sample '(D3/7: On Pace)'. _weekly_pace renders nothing of the kind - the real shape is like '3d14h/7d(4d2h) +21%'. Neither the D3/7 form nor the words On Pace appear anywhere in the module.
2. :67 says CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_USAGE_JSON skips get_claude_usage.py. The module is usage_api.py (covered by the rename sweep issue, listed here so the table is fixed in one pass).
3. CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_TIMESTAMP_EPOCH is read at statusline.py:991 and has no row in the table at all.

Also at :690, the _fetch_usage docstring summary reads 'env var -> cache bypass -> detached get_claude_usage.py'. There is no cache-bypass step: the path is env var, then one read of the cached usage row, return it if fresh, otherwise spawn a detached refresh and return the stale row anyway.
acceptance: The WEEKLY_PACE row shows a sample _weekly_pace can actually produce. A TIMESTAMP_EPOCH row exists and says what it pins. The USAGE_JSON row names usage_api. The _fetch_usage docstring summary describes the real three steps with no cache-bypass step.

title: Sweep pre-extraction module names out of comments and docs
Replace rot-prone literal counts and one-machine anecdotes
description:
Measured numbers from one developer's machine are stated as permanent facts. Several have already rotted, and two contradict each other inside a single file.

Already wrong:
  cache_db.py:538 - 'runs 15 IF NOT EXISTS statements, six ALTERs raising and catching duplicate column'. The real counts are 16 CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS statements and 21 _ADDED_COLUMNS entries, and both grow with every schema addition. This is the cost that justifies the SCHEMA_VERSION gate, so it understates the whole argument.
  ccreport.py:448-452 - NokCtx._rate_memo says 'Half a million records span a few hundred days'. docs/calculation-reference.md:378-383 already carries an erratum saying this overstates the real corpus (~89K rows) by ~5x. A doc that annotates another file's docstring is two things to keep in step; fix the docstring and delete the erratum.
  pricing.py:526 says '96 of 88,801 cached rows on a real machine'; pricing.py:1166 says 'all but two of ~105k cached records on a real machine'. Two different census figures in one file.

Repeated censuses:
  'four rows carrying it are in this table permanently' at cache_db.py:2887, ccreport.py:2299, docs:1140 and tests/test_ccreport.py:2523 - one machine's rate_limit_snapshots count, in four places. Any further placeholder row makes all four wrong at once.
  docs:378-383 - '~89K rows across ~1,560 files and 90 distinct days (measured 2026-08-07)'.
  tests/test_statusline.py:220 - 'across all 23 .dogcats repos in ~/git'.
  statusline.py:841 says ~/.claude.json is 'a quarter of a megabyte'; tests/test_statusline.py:1042 says '~258 KB'. Same file, two spellings, both drift as the file grows.

Moving literal counts:
  pyproject.toml:42, :106, :191 - '215 lines here run over 88 and 32 over 100', '200+ sites and no formatter to add them', 'answers with 5987 findings'.
  bin/ccreport:12 - 'all 109 KB is tokenized'; bin/statusline-command_x.sh:22 - 'the whole 92 KB is tokenized'.

In every case the durable point survives without the number. The bytecode-cache rationale is 'the whole module', not its size; the dedup rationale is 'a small minority', not 96.
acceptance: No comment or docstring in src/, tests/, tools/, bin/, docs/ or pyproject.toml states a row count, file count, byte size, finding count or line count measured from one machine. cache_db.py:538 describes the bootstrap shape rather than counting it. The NokCtx._rate_memo docstring carries no figure and the docs erratum paragraph is deleted. The four 'four rows' sites say that rows written before the lookahead check carry the placeholder. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Replace rot-prone literal counts and one-machine anecdotes
Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
description:
Six exported functions have behaviour that callers must handle and no docstring stating it. All are test-covered, so the behaviour is contract rather than accident.

1. pricing.compute_costs (pricing.py:1673) - the Cost buckets list documents 11 keys but the function returns 6 more (six_hour_project_cost through all_time_project_cost). It never states that session_window_cost is OMITTED rather than zeroed when no session reset is known - that omission is what statusline._merge_cost_data and usage_api._run_costs_only are built on, and zeroing it instead would carry the previous window's total across a rollover. The side effect (it caches the result via write_cost_summary) is also unstated.
2. ccreport.load_all_records (ccreport.py:802) - raises ValueError when use_rollups is passed together with since, until, project_filter or account_filter (ccreport.py:825-827). Undocumented.
3. cache_db.prefix_range (cache_db.py:1986) - raises ValueError on an empty prefix, with its own test. Undocumented. The reason is that an empty prefix would silently widen the range to the whole table.
4. ccreport.cmd_limits (ccreport.py:2540) - exits 1 when no samples exist and when the filters match nothing.
5. ccreport.cmd_adopt (ccreport.py:1917) - exits 1 when the capture log is empty.
6. cache_db.compute_extra_window_deltas (cache_db.py:1510) - never names the two keys it returns (extra_session_delta, extra_week_delta) or that None means no snapshot predates that window.

Smaller, same class: cache_db.usage_is_fresh, read_usage_cache and read_cost_summary (:1144, :1172, :3044) never say max_age is in seconds; usage_api.fetch_usage_api (:242) leaves its return contract at 'etc.' though the key set is _API_QUOTA_FIELDS and a test asserts the two are equal, and does not say HTTPError/URLError propagate once retries are exhausted.

Note: pyproject.toml disables D101/D102/D103/D107 deliberately so docstrings carry rationale rather than coverage. This issue is not about adding missing docstrings to internal helpers - it is about documented functions whose stated contract is incomplete.
acceptance: Each of the six carries the missing clause: compute_costs lists the project buckets, states the session_window_cost omission rule and the write_cost_summary side effect; load_all_records and prefix_range each have a Raises: ValueError line with the reason; cmd_limits and cmd_adopt each state when they exit 1; compute_extra_window_deltas names both keys and what None means. The three max_age docstrings say seconds. fetch_usage_api names _API_QUOTA_FIELDS instead of 'etc.' and states that HTTP and network errors propagate. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong
description:
This tree explains nearly every constant. These are the holes, each judged against its own neighbours in the same file.

1. cache_db.py:535 - PRAGMA cache_size = -2000. The comment explains only why the three pragmas sit outside the version gate, never that the negative sign is SQLite's KiB-versus-pages switch. 'Fixing' it to 2000 means 2000 pages, roughly 8 MB, per connection - on a path the status line opens every render.
2. ccreport.py:121 - CACHE_VERSION = 2 has no bump policy, while cache_db.SCHEMA_VERSION ('BUMP THIS on any change to...') and cache_db.CACHE_SCHEMA_SALT ('Bump this when...') both state theirs. It is also non-obviously not redundant with _script_hash(), which already hashes ccreport.py. So a maintainer either never bumps it or deletes it as dead weight.
3. The 10-minute usage TTL is spelled as a bare literal at four sites with nothing saying they must agree: usage_api.CACHE_MAX_AGE = 600, two max_age: int = 600 defaults in cache_db (:1172, :3044), and statusline.USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S = 600. That is a departure from this tree's rule of deriving key lists from one source and guarding drift with a test. Tuning one leaves the TTL check and the countdown the user reads describing different intervals.
4. statusline.py:125 - COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE = 900 is described as how long a cached compute_costs result stays usable, but nothing says it is what actually paces the costs-only refresh (via _fetch_usage's cost_summary is None branch), nor that the 300 s gap from USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S is deliberate. Aligning it to 600 changes how often a detached subprocess rescans the whole JSONL corpus.
5. cache_db.py:1203 - _BACKOFF_SCHEDULE = [45, 120, 240] names the unit and the index but gives no ceiling reasoning. Nothing says the last step must stay under the 600 s fetch interval; past that, one transient failure suppresses fetching indefinitely.
6. cache_db.py:43-44 - _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 10.0 and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT = 100 have no comment and are stranded under the legacy-paths block, so they read as belonging to it. The 10% is what decides whether real loss of unrebuildable orphan records gets reported.
7. cache_db.py:1503 - the 31-day snapshot prune. The comment restates the line and leaves 31 unexplained; the deltas this table feeds are the 5 h and 7 d windows, so 31 looks arbitrary. It is there because Extra usage is a monthly quota.
acceptance: Each of the seven carries a comment stating what breaks if the value moves, in this tree's existing style. The TTL item names one authority and says why the other three are spelled out rather than imported. _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT are moved out from under the legacy-paths block. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong
exchange.py: walkback rationale, _max_date, and a comment naming a deleted function
description:
Three prose defects in one module, worth fixing in one pass.

1. exchange.py:21 - _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS = 10 is bare, though it is read in six places: it bounds the cached read horizon in _load_cached_rates, the start of every fetch span in _fetch_span, and the get_rate loop. Its three immediate neighbours (_MIN_PLAUSIBLE_RATE, _NO_OBSERVATION, _OBSERVATION_SETTLE_DAYS) each get a full paragraph. A maintainer trimming it to 5 on the reasoning that a long weekend is 3 days makes an Easter or Christmas holiday cluster unresolvable: get_rate returns (None, False) and those records drop out of the NOK column with no error.
2. exchange.py:300 - get_rate documents both return values and the walkback thoroughly but never mentions its third parameter _max_date. It is what decides the estimated flag, and precomputing it once is the whole reason a per-record caller can afford this function.
3. exchange.py:23 and tests/test_exchange.py:231 both explain themselves in terms of _find_missing_range, which no longer exists. The function is _fetch_span.

Also here, though it belongs to the restatement cleanup: exchange.py:316-319 repeats the estimated-at-the-trailing-edge rule that the docstring at :303-306 already states, inside a nine-line function.
acceptance: _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS carries a comment naming what it bounds and what silently breaks if it is lowered. get_rate's docstring documents _max_date and why it is passed in. grep for _find_missing_range across the repo returns nothing. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: exchange.py: walkback rationale, _max_date, and a comment naming a deleted function
One rationale is re-argued at every observer instead of stated once
description:
Three constraints are each told in full at many sites. Every individual copy carries a real fact - this is verbosity, not error, so the fix is to keep the canonical statement where the constraint is enforced and leave the observers with a bare pointer. Do not delete the rationale.

1. Rate-limit reset drift, the 9999999999 placeholder, and 'never pruned' - told in full at cache_db.py:304-328 (the CREATE TABLE), RL_MAX_LOOKAHEAD_S (:2884-2892), rl_window_key (:2896-2921), record_rate_limit_snapshots (:2939+), load_rate_limit_snapshots (:2997+), statusline._rl_sample (:875+), ccreport._implausible_reset (:2295+), ccreport._window_instances (:2127+), AGENTS.md:98-114 and docs section 9.6. The same drift observation appears verbatim in three of them.
2. Account capture and attribution - cache_db's CREATE TABLE, record_account_event, AGENTS.md:80-97, statusline._capture_account, and docs 9.1 through 9.5.
3. The snapshot deferral - cache_db.py:805-828, _daily_snapshot_deferred, _refresh_env, statusline.main, ccreport.main and two test class docstrings.

Individual over-length sites worth trimming in the same pass:

  pricing.py:1286-1310 - a 25-line docstring for two facts; the caching story is already docs 5.6.
  statusline.py:833-851 - trim the first two paragraphs, replace the third with one best-effort line.
  docs:1050-1065 - the four-bullet reasoning-in-both-directions passage plus 'That is intended, not a regression' becomes one sentence.
