title: One rationale is re-argued at every observer instead of stated once
Delete comments that restate the line below them, and label-only dividers
description:
About 50 sites where the prose adds nothing the code does not already say. pyproject.toml disables D103 precisely so docstrings can carry rationale rather than coverage, so these run against the project's own stated norm and bury the real comments around them.

Restatement, one comment per statement:
  ccreport.py:2763 - 'No subcommand: show daily + monthly summary'. The else branch already says no subcommand, and the block calls report_daily, report_monthly, report_project, report_session and conditionally report_account - the comment names two of five.
  ccreport.py:1427, 1466, 1534, 1626, 492, 562, 1167, 1177, 1188, 1300, 1336 - eleven docstrings that are the function name with spaces added. Keep fmt_tokens, fmt_cost, _fmt_cache_read and short_model, which state a threshold or show sample output.
  ccreport.py:553, 555 - one comment per line of a five-line function whose docstring already shows the transformation.
  cache_db.py:1563, 1569, 1577 (load_cost_cache); :1472, 1495, 1503; :2083, 2088; :1127 (restates _USAGE_COLS six lines above - keep the '# skip id column' below it, which explains the +1).
  statusline.py:257, 270, 313, 354, 1371, 1382 - six docstrings restating name plus return annotation; _extra_deltas and _ustr have docstrings longer than their bodies. Keep _collect_battery and _get_terminal_cols, which state a shape and an order.
  statusline.py:1252 - 'Remaining time until reset' over remain_s = int(reset_epoch - now).
  usage_api.py:153, 158, 287. Keep the neighbouring '# API returns cents; convert to dollars', which carries a unit.
  pricing.py:449, 1928, 1830.
  exchange.py:316-319 - a verbatim repeat of the docstring twelve lines above.

Label-only dividers:
  statusline.py:115-117 - two labels for the same block, two lines apart; delete the first.
  statusline.py:1753 - '# --- Main ---' over ~600 lines holding the cost merge, input parsing, layout, the fetch cache and main(). Delete or name what it holds.
  ccu.py:338-340 - '# Entry point' in a file already ending in if __name__ == __main__.
  usage_api.py:300-302 - '# Main' over a 220-line grab-bag.
  usage_api.py:66 - 'HTTP status codes worth retrying' over _RETRYABLE_STATUS.
  pricing.py:1807 and :1822 - dividers restating the docstring and the call directly beneath them.
  tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:129, 133, 156 - phase dividers duplicating the log() call on the next line.
  tests/test_pricing.py - 23 divider blocks (46 comment lines) in a 2,757-line module; twelve are pure label restatement of the class immediately below. The divider count is the file asking to be split into modules; if the split is deferred, delete those twelve.

Deliberately protected - do not touch: cache_db.py's 15 section dividers (several carry load-bearing prose), statusline.py's per-segment dividers which navigate a 2,376-line file, tests/test_exchange.py's five dividers grouping module-level functions, and the aligned trailing comments on schema columns and constants, which carry units, sentinel meanings and NULL semantics.
acceptance: The listed restatements and label-only dividers are deleted. Where a comment carried even one real clause, that clause is folded into the docstring rather than dropped. Every protected item above is untouched. just lint-all and just test pass.

title: Delete comments that restate the line below them, and label-only dividers
Four prose nits that state no checkable property
description:
None of these carries a wrong fact, so none needs deleting - each needs rewording.

1. statusline.py:1 - 'Claude Code status line - Python implementation for performance'. No checkable property; residue from the shell-to-Python rewrite. The real facts (renders on every frame, imports nothing outside the stdlib, defers cache_db into the functions that touch it) are stated further down and in AGENTS.md. Either shorten to the bare title or state the property.
2. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 - 'Seam Claude Code settings.json points at'. The tree calls this a wrapper everywhere else: README.md ('Point Claude Code settings.json at the wrapper'), bin/ccreport:2 ('A wrapper rather than a symlink'), AGENTS.md ('bin/ holds the wrappers'). One file renames the thing. Note that ccu.py:9's use of 'seam' is precise - it names the boundary the tests stub - and should stay.
3. exchange.py:3-4 - 'Fetches from the Norges Bank SDMX-JSON API, caches in SQLite, and provides rate lookups with automatic fallback for weekends and holidays'. The third item restates the first two; 'provides rate lookups' dodges a plain verb and 'automatic' adds nothing a caller can act on.
4. justfile:13 - '# run all formatters' above fmt-all: just fmt. There is exactly one, and AGENTS.md explicitly forbids adding a second ('Do not add ruff format to a recipe'). The plural invites the edit the project rules out.
acceptance: Each of the four is reworded. statusline.py:1 either states a property or is a bare title. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 says wrapper; ccu.py:9 is untouched. exchange.py's module docstring names what get_rate does in plain verbs. justfile:13 says there is deliberately one formatter.

title: Four prose nits that state no checkable property
just bench resolves a path that does not exist, so it fails on every run
description:
tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:39 sets STATUSLINE = HERE / 'statusline_command.py', which resolves to tools/statusline_command.py. That file does not exist - the module is src/ccreport/statusline.py, renamed during the macsetup to ccreport extraction. main() hits the 'if not STATUSLINE.exists()' guard, prints 'missing ...' and returns 1, so just bench has never worked in this repo.

Not a one-line path swap. The benchmark invokes the target as an executable, [str(STATUSLINE), '-t'], so whatever replaces it must be runnable that way. bin/statusline-command_x.sh is the wrapper Claude Code itself points at and is the obvious candidate; running the module directly would need a python -m ccreport.statusline invocation instead, which changes what the benchmark measures - the wrapper's bytecode-cache behaviour is part of the cost the benchmark exists to report.

Found during the comment-cop documentation sweep. The docstring references at :5 and :17 were already corrected under ccreport-5yve; only the path is left.
acceptance: just bench runs to completion and reports timings. The chosen target is runnable as an executable and measures the same path Claude Code actually invokes on a render. A test covers the resolution so the path cannot rot silently again.

Weekly pace label says 7d while the delta is computed against pace_days()
description:
src/ccreport/statusline.py _weekly_pace emits a hardcoded /7d in its label - f'{elapsed_str}/7d({cd})' and f'{elapsed_str}/7d' - while the expected percentage it compares against is computed from pricing.pace_days(), which reads CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS and defaults to 7.

With CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS set to anything other than 7, the status line shows an elapsed fraction labelled against a 7-day window while the +/-N% delta beside it is paced against a shorter one. The two halves of the same segment then describe different windows, and nothing on screen says so.

README documents CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS as a supported knob, and ccu.pace_line uses pace_days() consistently for both the divisor and its printed '(pace: Nd)' fragment - so ccu and the status line disagree with each other for any non-default value.

Two readings, and the fix differs:
- The literal is the real week window and only the delta is paced. Then the label is right and the docstring's {N} placeholder is what is wrong.
- The label should follow the knob. Then the literal should be the pace value, matching what ccu prints.

Found during the comment-cop documentation sweep; the docstring was left alone pending this decision.
acceptance: The label and the delta describe the same window for every value of CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS, or the segment states both windows explicitly. ccu.pace_line and the status line agree for a non-default value. A test sets CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS to something other than 7 and asserts the rendered segment.

docs section 5.5 describes the pre-incremental session cache
description:
docs/calculation-reference.md:443-455 says the session cost fingerprint is an md5 over the sorted (path, mtime_ns, size) tuples, and that a session is re-parsed whenever any file's mtime or size changes.

The code does something else. pricing._encode_session_state stores a versioned JSON blob: a version field, a per-file _FileCursor (mtime_ns, size, offset, tail) and dedup-key digests. pricing._decode_session_state:897 names the md5 shape explicitly as 'the pre-incremental md5 fingerprint' - the legacy form it still reads. A file that grew is resumed from its stored offset and tail digest, not re-parsed from the top.

Why it matters: the doc describes full invalidation where the code does incremental resume. A maintainer chasing a wrong session cost looks for the wrong failure mode, and the real one (a cursor that drifted from the file) is not documented at all.
acceptance: Section 5.5 rewritten around _SessionCostState and _SESSION_STATE_VERSION: what the blob holds, that a version mismatch costs one full reparse, that growth is resumed from offset plus the tail digest, and that the md5 form is legacy read-only. description:
Six exported functions have behaviour that callers must handle and no docstring stating it. All are test-covered, so the behaviour is contract rather than accident.

1. pricing.compute_costs (pricing.py:1673) - the Cost buckets list documents 11 keys but the function returns 6 more (six_hour_project_cost through all_time_project_cost). It never states that session_window_cost is OMITTED rather than zeroed when no session reset is known - that omission is what statusline._merge_cost_data and usage_api._run_costs_only are built on, and zeroing it instead would carry the previous window's total across a rollover. The side effect (it caches the result via write_cost_summary) is also unstated.
2. ccreport.load_all_records (ccreport.py:802) - raises ValueError when use_rollups is passed together with since, until, project_filter or account_filter (ccreport.py:825-827). Undocumented.
3. cache_db.prefix_range (cache_db.py:1986) - raises ValueError on an empty prefix, with its own test. Undocumented. The reason is that an empty prefix would silently widen the range to the whole table.
4. ccreport.cmd_limits (ccreport.py:2540) - exits 1 when no samples exist and when the filters match nothing.
5. ccreport.cmd_adopt (ccreport.py:1917) - exits 1 when the capture log is empty.
6. cache_db.compute_extra_window_deltas (cache_db.py:1510) - never names the two keys it returns (extra_session_delta, extra_week_delta) or that None means no snapshot predates that window.

Smaller, same class: cache_db.usage_is_fresh, read_usage_cache and read_cost_summary (:1144, :1172, :3044) never say max_age is in seconds; usage_api.fetch_usage_api (:242) leaves its return contract at 'etc.' though the key set is _API_QUOTA_FIELDS and a test asserts the two are equal, and does not say HTTPError/URLError propagate once retries are exhausted.

Note: pyproject.toml disables D101/D102/D103/D107 deliberately so docstrings carry rationale rather than coverage. This issue is not about adding missing docstrings to internal helpers - it is about documented functions whose stated contract is incomplete.

title: Document the contracts of the public surface: raises, exits, return shapes
Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong
description:
This tree explains nearly every constant. These are the holes, each judged against its own neighbours in the same file.

1. cache_db.py:535 - PRAGMA cache_size = -2000. The comment explains only why the three pragmas sit outside the version gate, never that the negative sign is SQLite's KiB-versus-pages switch. 'Fixing' it to 2000 means 2000 pages, roughly 8 MB, per connection - on a path the status line opens every render.
2. ccreport.py:121 - CACHE_VERSION = 2 has no bump policy, while cache_db.SCHEMA_VERSION ('BUMP THIS on any change to...') and cache_db.CACHE_SCHEMA_SALT ('Bump this when...') both state theirs. It is also non-obviously not redundant with _script_hash(), which already hashes ccreport.py. So a maintainer either never bumps it or deletes it as dead weight.
3. The 10-minute usage TTL is spelled as a bare literal at four sites with nothing saying they must agree: usage_api.CACHE_MAX_AGE = 600, two max_age: int = 600 defaults in cache_db (:1172, :3044), and statusline.USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S = 600. That is a departure from this tree's rule of deriving key lists from one source and guarding drift with a test. Tuning one leaves the TTL check and the countdown the user reads describing different intervals.
4. statusline.py:125 - COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE = 900 is described as how long a cached compute_costs result stays usable, but nothing says it is what actually paces the costs-only refresh (via _fetch_usage's cost_summary is None branch), nor that the 300 s gap from USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S is deliberate. Aligning it to 600 changes how often a detached subprocess rescans the whole JSONL corpus.
5. cache_db.py:1203 - _BACKOFF_SCHEDULE = [45, 120, 240] names the unit and the index but gives no ceiling reasoning. Nothing says the last step must stay under the 600 s fetch interval; past that, one transient failure suppresses fetching indefinitely.
6. cache_db.py:43-44 - _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 10.0 and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT = 100 have no comment and are stranded under the legacy-paths block, so they read as belonging to it. The 10% is what decides whether real loss of unrebuildable orphan records gets reported.
7. cache_db.py:1503 - the 31-day snapshot prune. The comment restates the line and leaves 31 unexplained; the deltas this table feeds are the 5 h and 7 d windows, so 31 looks arbitrary. It is there because Extra usage is a monthly quota.
acceptance: Each of the seven carries a comment stating what breaks if the value moves, in this tree's existing style. The TTL item names one authority and says why the other three are spelled out rather than imported. _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT are moved out from under the legacy-paths block. just lint-all and just test pass.

description:
Three prose defects in one module, worth fixing in one pass.

1. exchange.py:21 - _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS = 10 is bare, though it is read in six places: it bounds the cached read horizon in _load_cached_rates, the start of every fetch span in _fetch_span, and the get_rate loop. Its three immediate neighbours (_MIN_PLAUSIBLE_RATE, _NO_OBSERVATION, _OBSERVATION_SETTLE_DAYS) each get a full paragraph. A maintainer trimming it to 5 on the reasoning that a long weekend is 3 days makes an Easter or Christmas holiday cluster unresolvable: get_rate returns (None, False) and those records drop out of the NOK column with no error.
2. exchange.py:300 - get_rate documents both return values and the walkback thoroughly but never mentions its third parameter _max_date. It is what decides the estimated flag, and precomputing it once is the whole reason a per-record caller can afford this function.
3. exchange.py:23 and tests/test_exchange.py:231 both explain themselves in terms of _find_missing_range, which no longer exists. The function is _fetch_span.

Also here, though it belongs to the restatement cleanup: exchange.py:316-319 repeats the estimated-at-the-trailing-edge rule that the docstring at :303-306 already states, inside a nine-line function.
acceptance: _MAX_WALKBACK_DAYS carries a comment naming what it bounds and what silently breaks if it is lowered. get_rate's docstring documents _max_date and why it is passed in. grep for _find_missing_range across the repo returns nothing. just lint-all and just test pass.

description:
Three constraints are each told in full at many sites. Every individual copy carries a real fact - this is verbosity, not error, so the fix is to keep the canonical statement where the constraint is enforced and leave the observers with a bare pointer. Do not delete the rationale.

description:

  statusline.py:257, 270, 313, 354, 1371, 1382 - six docstrings restating name plus return annotation; _extra_deltas and _ustr have docstrings longer than their bodies. Keep _collect_battery and _get_terminal_cols, which state a shape and an order.

  usage_api.py:153, 158, 287. Keep the neighbouring '# API returns cents; convert to dollars', which carries a unit.
  pricing.py:449, 1928, 1830.
  exchange.py:316-319 - a verbatim repeat of the docstring twelve lines above.

  statusline.py:1753 - '# --- Main ---' over ~600 lines holding the cost merge, input parsing, layout, the fetch cache and main(). Delete or name what it holds.
  ccu.py:338-340 - '# Entry point' in a file already ending in if __name__ == __main__.
  usage_api.py:300-302 - '# Main' over a 220-line grab-bag.

Four prose nits that state no checkable property
description:
None of these carries a wrong fact, so none needs deleting - each needs rewording.

1. statusline.py:1 - 'Claude Code status line - Python implementation for performance'. No checkable property; residue from the shell-to-Python rewrite. The real facts (renders on every frame, imports nothing outside the stdlib, defers cache_db into the functions that touch it) are stated further down and in AGENTS.md. Either shorten to the bare title or state the property.
2. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 - 'Seam Claude Code settings.json points at'. The tree calls this a wrapper everywhere else: README.md ('Point Claude Code settings.json at the wrapper'), bin/ccreport:2 ('A wrapper rather than a symlink'), AGENTS.md ('bin/ holds the wrappers'). One file renames the thing. Note that ccu.py:9's use of 'seam' is precise - it names the boundary the tests stub - and should stay.
3. exchange.py:3-4 - 'Fetches from the Norges Bank SDMX-JSON API, caches in SQLite, and provides rate lookups with automatic fallback for weekends and holidays'. The third item restates the first two; 'provides rate lookups' dodges a plain verb and 'automatic' adds nothing a caller can act on.
4. justfile:13 - '# run all formatters' above fmt-all: just fmt. There is exactly one, and AGENTS.md explicitly forbids adding a second ('Do not add ruff format to a recipe'). The plural invites the edit the project rules out.
acceptance: Each of the four is reworded. statusline.py:1 either states a property or is a bare title. bin/statusline-command_x.sh:2 says wrapper; ccu.py:9 is untouched. exchange.py's module docstring names what get_rate does in plain verbs. justfile:13 says there is deliberately one formatter.

title: Four prose nits that state no checkable property
Weekly pace label says 7d while the delta is computed against pace_days()
description:
src/ccreport/statusline.py _weekly_pace emits a hardcoded /7d in its label - f'{elapsed_str}/7d({cd})' and f'{elapsed_str}/7d' - while the expected percentage it compares against is computed from pricing.pace_days(), which reads CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS and defaults to 7.

With CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS set to anything other than 7, the status line shows an elapsed fraction labelled against a 7-day window while the +/-N% delta beside it is paced against a shorter one. The two halves of the same segment then describe different windows, and nothing on screen says so.

README documents CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS as a supported knob, and ccu.pace_line uses pace_days() consistently for both the divisor and its printed '(pace: Nd)' fragment - so ccu and the status line disagree with each other for any non-default value.

Two readings, and the fix differs:
- The literal is the real week window and only the delta is paced. Then the label is right and the docstring's {N} placeholder is what is wrong.
- The label should follow the knob. Then the literal should be the pace value, matching what ccu prints.

Found during the comment-cop documentation sweep; the docstring was left alone pending this decision.
acceptance: The label and the delta describe the same window for every value of CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS, or the segment states both windows explicitly. ccu.pace_line and the status line agree for a non-default value. A test sets CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS to something other than 7 and asserts the rendered segment.

just bench resolves a path that does not exist, so it fails on every run
description:
tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:39 sets STATUSLINE = HERE / 'statusline_command.py', which resolves to tools/statusline_command.py. That file does not exist - the module is src/ccreport/statusline.py, renamed during the macsetup to ccreport extraction. main() hits the 'if not STATUSLINE.exists()' guard, prints 'missing ...' and returns 1, so just bench has never worked in this repo.

Not a one-line path swap. The benchmark invokes the target as an executable, [str(STATUSLINE), '-t'], so whatever replaces it must be runnable that way. bin/statusline-command_x.sh is the wrapper Claude Code itself points at and is the obvious candidate; running the module directly would need a python -m ccreport.statusline invocation instead, which changes what the benchmark measures - the wrapper's bytecode-cache behaviour is part of the cost the benchmark exists to report.

Found during the comment-cop documentation sweep. The docstring references at :5 and :17 were already corrected under ccreport-5yve; only the path is left.
acceptance: just bench runs to completion and reports timings. The chosen target is runnable as an executable and measures the same path Claude Code actually invokes on a render. A test covers the resolution so the path cannot rot silently again.

extra_reset is declared and rendered but never written
description:
usage_api.fetch_usage_api never sets extra_reset, yet cache_db declares the column and ccu.py:331 renders it as the reset line for Extra usage. So that line can only ever show a value some other path wrote, and on the normal fetch path it has nothing to show.

Either the API response carries a reset for the Extra quota under a field name the mapper does not pick up, in which case fetch_usage_api should map it, or it does not, in which case the column and the render are dead weight and ccu should stop drawing a line it can never fill.

Found during the comment-cop documentation sweep. docs/calculation-reference.md now documents the gap rather than describing a value that gets written, so whichever way this resolves the doc needs a matching edit.
acceptance: Either fetch_usage_api populates extra_reset from the API response and ccu renders it, or the column and its render are removed. docs/calculation-reference.md matches whichever holds, with the gap paragraph deleted. A test covers the resulting behaviour.

Status line: show signed-in username and organization on the last line
description:
Nothing on the status line names which account the session bills to, so a /login switch between the personal Max org and a work org is invisible while working.

Add a segment on the last line (line 4 in the narrow layout) fed by the newest account_events row (cache_db.read_latest_account()), which the render already captures via _capture_account. Two independent toggles, both default off, in the style of CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_BATTERY:

- CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_USER — the signed-in emailAddress, e.g. post@rykroken.net
- CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_ORG — organizationName, e.g. "post@rykroken.net's Organization"

Both on renders 'post@rykroken.net (post@rykroken.net's Organization)'; ORG alone renders the org name bare. Neither on must cost no database read.

Files: src/ccreport/statusline.py (new _render_account, _Fetched gains a field so _FAST_CACHE_SCHEMA must be bumped, _layout_and_print appends to the last line, env-var table in the module docstring), docs/calculation-reference.md if the segment list lives there.

Acceptance: both toggles off render the line exactly as today; each toggle on alone renders its own field; both on render the pair; an empty account_events table renders nothing rather than parentheses; tests under tests/ cover the four toggle combinations and the no-capture case.

README: document a personal statusline wrapper
description:
README.md points settings.json straight at bin/statusline-command_x.sh, which is tracked in git. Users who set CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_* there get a dirty working tree and a conflict on every pull.

statusline-command_x.sh already reads every toggle as ${VAR:-default} (bin/statusline-command_x.sh:5-13), so an outer wrapper that exports the vars and execs it wins. Document that shape in the Status line section: a small untracked script the user owns, settings.json pointing at it, and "$@" passed through.
acceptance: README.md's Status line section shows a copy-pasteable wrapper script exporting CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_* and exec-ing bin/statusline-command_x.sh with "$@", plus the settings.json snippet pointing at the user's wrapper. Points at src/ccreport/statusline.py's docstring for the full toggle list.

description:
Nothing on the status line names which account the session bills to, so a /login switch between the personal Max org and a work org is invisible while working.

Add a segment on the last line (line 4 in the narrow layout) fed by the newest account_events row (cache_db.read_latest_account()), which the render already captures via _capture_account. Two independent toggles, both default off, in the style of CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_BATTERY:

- CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_USER — the signed-in emailAddress, e.g. post@rykroken.net
- CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_ORG — organizationName, e.g. "post@rykroken.net's Organization"

Both on renders 'post@rykroken.net (post@rykroken.net's Organization)'; ORG alone renders the org name bare. Neither on must cost no database read.

Statusline DSP badge missing after --resume with the flag
description:
A DSP verdict of False is memoized for the session id's whole life, but the
verdict only holds for one claude process. `--resume` reuses the session id, so
a session first launched without --dangerously-skip-permissions and restarted
with it never shows the badge.

Chain, in src/ccreport/statusline.py:

- The non-DSP launch writes {"dsp": false} to the per-session memo (_memo_path,
  keyed by session_id in TMPDIR).
- The resumed claude resolves the same memo path.
- _start_dsp_check (:432) returns None when `memoized is not None`, and
  False is not None, so `ps -Aww` never spawns again.
- _collect_dsp returns None, and :2267 falls back to memo.get("dsp", False).

Observed on session 9039cf27-6302-4b0c-8be4-33083d6ee07e, running as
`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --resume 9039cf27-...` with a memo
holding {"dsp": false}. Running the ancestor walk live from a child of that
session returns True, so detection itself is correct.

Only a True verdict is safe to memoize permanently. A False one needs
invalidating when the ancestor claude process changes.

Workaround: delete the session's .memo.json from TMPDIR.

comments.text:
Fixed outside this repo: a SessionStart hook clears the memo instead of the
statusline re-checking on a timer. No statusline.py logic change.

- claude/hooks/clear-statusline-memo.sh — reads session_id from the hook JSON,
  deletes $TMPDIR/claude-statusline-<uid>-<sid>.memo.json, prints nothing
  (SessionStart stdout lands in the session context).
- SessionStart matcher startup|resume|clear|compact added to both profile
  settings.json files (mbp2022, sbnorge).

it. Full suite passes (984).

ids including traversal input and an 80-character id. Not yet verified in a live
resume — the hook loads at session start, so the running sessions predate it.

comments.text:
Correction to the previous comment, after reading the hooks reference:

- SessionStart takes no matcher — the field is silently ignored, and the
  sources include "fork" as well. Both settings.json entries now omit it.

  line, `bash $HOME/git/ccreport/bin/clear-statusline-memo.sh`.

statusline-command_x.sh, not in macsetup's hooks/ — it belongs to the status
line, and macsetup only wires it. tests/test_statusline.py asserts the hook
deletes exactly what _memo_path writes, over four session ids; nothing else
would catch the two constructions drifting apart. README.md documents the hook
for anyone installing the status line. Suite: 988 pass, ruff and pyright clean.

Make Sonnet 5's $2/$10 pricing permanent
description:
Anthropic made Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing ($2 input / $10 output per MTok) permanent. Verified 2026-08-12 against https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md, which lists Sonnet 5 at '$2 / input MTok $10 / output MTok' with no introductory qualifier and no end date.

src/ccreport/pricing.py currently encodes the intro rate as a 2026-06-01 period and reverts to $3/$15 in a 2026-09-01 period that must be deleted:

- PRICING_HISTORY entry effective '2026-09-01' (claude-sonnet-5 at 3e-06/15e-06) — delete it entirely.
- The 2026-06-01 entry's comment says 'introductory pricing ... through 2026-08-31' — reword; the rate is now permanent.
- LAST_CHECKED — bump to 2026-08-12.

Nothing else changes: cache_create/cache_read stay at 2.5e-06/0.2e-06 (1.25x/0.1x of input), and no other model's prices move. Because _script_hash() covers pricing.py and the rollup fingerprint hashes it too, the corpus re-parses and ccreport_rollups rebuild on their own.

Acceptance: no period in PRICING_HISTORY prices claude-sonnet-5 above 2e-06/10e-06 at any timestamp; 'just lint-all' and 'just test' pass.

Status line reports when the ccreport checkout is behind origin
description:
The status line should print a line under the cost-window line when the local ccreport checkout is behind GitHub's master.

Target render, under `24H $14/$417 · 7D $154/$1963 · 30D $154/$10259 · AT $154/$12587`:

    ↑ 12 commits behind · git pull

Decisions taken with the user (2026-08-12):

- No tags, no GitHub releases, no PyPI. master is the release; `version` in pyproject.toml stays a placeholder nobody reads. The unit of 'update available' is a commit.
- The remote state comes from the GitHub REST API, not from git. No fetch, nothing written into the user's .git, and it works when the checkout has no usable remote credentials.
- The check runs twice a day (12 h TTL), from a detached process on the slow render path, never inline. A network call on the render path is the one thing the status line's whole design avoids.

The endpoint is the compare API, which answers ancestry and count in one request:

    GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master

It returns `status` (behind | ahead | identical | diverged) and `ahead_by`. `status == 'ahead'` means master is ahead of the local commit by `ahead_by` commits, which is the number to render. Unauthenticated the API allows 60 requests per hour per IP; this spends 2 per day.

Children carry the work. Nothing here is implemented yet.

title: Status line reports when the ccreport checkout is behind origin
update_check.py: ask GitHub how far master is ahead of the local commit
description:
New module `src/ccreport/update_check.py`, run as a detached subprocess (`python3 -m ccreport.update_check`), never imported by a render.

What it does, in order:

1. Find the checkout root from its own location: `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`. If there is no `.git` directory there, exit 0 and write nothing — the user installed with `uv tool install .` and has no checkout to update.
2. Read the local HEAD SHA. Prefer parsing `.git/HEAD` plus the ref file (and `.git/packed-refs` as fallback) over forking git, so the same helper can serve the render path.
3. Derive owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin` — do not hardcode oroddlokken/ccreport, a fork has its own. Accept both `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` and `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`.
4. GET `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master` with urllib, `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, timeout 10 s. Follow the pattern already in `src/ccreport/exchange.py:131`.
5. Write to the `meta` table (`src/ccreport/cache_db.py:55`, helpers `_get_meta` at :3067 and `_set_meta` at :3091): the local SHA it compared, the commits-ahead count, and the epoch stamp of the check.

Failure is silence. A 404 (the local commit is not on GitHub — an unpushed commit, which is the normal state for whoever develops this), a network error, a rate-limit 403, a body that does not parse: write the stamp so the 12 h TTL still advances, write no count, exit 0. Nothing this module does may ever surface as an error on a render.

Storing the local SHA alongside the count is what keeps the render honest: if the user pulls, the render sees its own SHA no longer matches the compared one and suppresses the line until the next check, rather than claiming a stale 'behind'.

Acceptance: tests under `tests/` covering the SSH and HTTPS remote-URL forms, the loose-ref and packed-refs HEAD reads, a mocked 'ahead' response writing the count, and each failure mode writing the stamp but no count.

Spawn the update check from the slow render path on a 12 h TTL
description:
Wire `ccreport.update_check` into `src/ccreport/statusline.py` so it runs twice a day and costs a render nothing.

Follow `_spawn_usage_refresh` at `src/ccreport/statusline.py:659`: `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` with stdout and stderr to DEVNULL, so it outlives the render that started it.

Gate:

- Slow renders only. The fast path (`FAST_TTL_S`, 15 s, `_Fetched`) must not spawn it, and must not re-read the meta row — the rendered segment belongs in the fast cache next to the other rendered segments.
- Spawn only when `now - update_checked_at >= 43200` (12 h). Put the constant beside the other TTLs, not inline.
- The stamp is written by the child even on failure, so a repo with no network spawns one process per 12 h, not one per render.

Acceptance: a test asserting no spawn when the stamp is fresh, one spawn when it is 12 h old, and none at all on a fast-path render.

title: Document the update check in README and AGENTS.md
Status line reports when the ccreport checkout is behind origin
description:
The status line should print a line under the cost-window line when the local ccreport checkout is behind GitHub's master.

Target render, under `24H $14/$417 · 7D $154/$1963 · 30D $154/$10259 · AT $154/$12587`:

    ↑ 12 commits behind · git pull

Decisions taken with the user (2026-08-12):

- No tags, no GitHub releases, no PyPI. master is the release; `version` in pyproject.toml stays a placeholder nobody reads. The unit of 'update available' is a commit.
- The remote state comes from the GitHub REST API, not from git. No fetch, nothing written into the user's .git, and it works when the checkout has no usable remote credentials.
- The check runs twice a day (12 h TTL), from a detached process on the slow render path, never inline. A network call on the render path is the one thing the status line's whole design avoids.

The endpoint is the compare API, which answers ancestry and count in one request:

    GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master

It returns `status` (behind | ahead | identical | diverged) and `ahead_by`. `status == 'ahead'` means master is ahead of the local commit by `ahead_by` commits, which is the number to render. Unauthenticated the API allows 60 requests per hour per IP; this spends 2 per day.

Children carry the work. Nothing here is implemented yet.

Statusline: show the scoped model quota when a subagent used that model
description:
Today the per-model weekly quota segment (S/W/Fa in the rate-limit group) is gated on the *selected* model only. In statusline.py _render_rate_limits:

    sc_wanted = sc_mode == 'always' or (
        sc_mode == 'current' and sc_model.lower() in _ustr(usage, '_current_model').lower()
    )

_current_model is inp.model, the display name Claude Code sends on stdin. So a session running Opus that dispatched Fable subagents burns the Fable weekly quota while the Fable segment stays hidden until SCOPED_MODE=always.

Subagent traffic is logged in the session's own JSONL (verified: ~/.claude/projects/.../09a9e5e9-*.jsonl carries 89 claude-fable-5 and 112 claude-opus-5 assistant records), and pricing._find_session_files already includes the <session_id>/ subdirectory, so the models a session actually used are available from the same scan that computes the session cost.

Plan:
- pricing.py: _scan_session_file already gets the model from _line_cost; accumulate pricing.model_family(model) per scan. Carry the set on _SessionCostState, persist it in the state blob (_encode/_decode_session_state, bump _SESSION_STATE_VERSION so old blobs reparse once), merge it in _resume_session_cost, and derive it in _purged_session_cost from the cached records' model field. Expose it next to the cost without a second parse.
- statusline.py: carry the families on _Fetched (bump _FAST_CACHE_SCHEMA) and widen the SCOPED_MODE=current gate to model_family(sc_model) in those families.
- docs/calculation-reference.md section on the scoped segment (~line 790) and the CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_SCOPED_MODE help text in statusline.py describe 'current model' — update both.

ccreport update: report how far behind master the checkout is, --pull to fast-forward
description:
The status line already renders '↑ N commits behind · git pull' from update_check.py, but there is no way to ask for that answer from the CLI. Add a 'ccreport update' subcommand.

Behaviour:
- Runs the check live (update_check.checkout_root/local_head_sha/remote_slug/commits_behind) rather than reading cache_db.read_update_check(), because a CLI invocation is not a render and the user asked now. Store the fresh result via cache_db.write_update_check() so the status line's stamp and count are refreshed too.
- Prints one of: not a git checkout (installed as a package), up to date, N commit(s) behind plus the 'git pull' hint, or 'could not check' when the API/remote did not answer.
- With --pull, and only when behind > 0, runs 'git pull --ff-only' in the checkout and prints its outcome. Never a merge, never a rebase.
- Runs before the record-loading path in main(), like migrate/overrides/limits/adopt do: it needs no corpus and has no report to print.

Files: src/ccreport/ccreport.py (cmd_update + subparser + early dispatch), tests/test_ccreport.py or a new tests/test_update_command.py, docs/calculation-reference.md and AGENTS.md if the update-check paragraph needs it.
acceptance:
- 'ccreport update' prints the live behind-count and exits 0 in every outcome including a failed check.
- 'ccreport update --pull' fast-forwards only when behind > 0 and reports what git did.
- A checkout with no .git (installed package) prints that and does not call the API.
- pytest covers: up-to-date, behind, no-checkout, unanswered check, --pull when up to date, --pull when behind.
- just lint-all and just test pass.

ccreport limits: mark window instances whose sampling started late
description:
The week window ending 2026-08-11 18:00 opened at 2026-08-04 18:00 but the first stored snapshot is 2026-08-08 13:27 at 77% (src/ccreport/ccreport.py, rate_limit_snapshots). Capture starts when a render happens, so 4 days and 77 points went unobserved.

The report prints 'seen from 77%', but the table's Peak, Spend and $/pp read as whole-window numbers when they cover the sampled span only: that instance shows $458 and $29/pp while the real week spend was ~$2400.

Wanted: in `ccreport limits`, detect an instance whose first sample lands materially after the window start (start = resets_at - window span, from pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS) and mark it in the table, so a partial instance is not read as a complete one. No snapshot rows are added or deleted; percentages are never synthesized.
acceptance: A window instance whose first sample is well after its start renders a visible partial marker; a fully observed instance renders unchanged; pytest covers both cases.

ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts
description:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions already taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups.
- Read surface: server-side CLI. ccreport renders tables the server computed. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one shared bearer token over HTTPS.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at most every 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push.

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps account and machine onto each record before sending.
- Each record carries its cost frozen at push time, the way ccreport_rollups already freezes cost, so the server never re-prices and pricing.py drift between machines cannot rewrite history.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py.

Children: server package and schema, ingest endpoint and auth, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI.

Server package: FastAPI factory, Granian entry, merged SQLite schema
description:
Create src/ccreport/server/ holding the FastAPI app and its own SQLite database, separate from ~/.cache/ccreport/cache.db. The client cache stays a per-machine artifact; the server database is the merged one.

Follow ~/git/kantine: an app factory create_app() (src/km2/web/factory.py), a Granian entry point taking host/port/workers (src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py), and a justfile recipe. Add fastapi and granian with uv add, so uv.lock records them. Keep them out of the status line import path: statusline.py must still import stdlib only.

Schema, in a new module mirroring cache_db.py style (one column tuple driving SELECT, INSERT and row mapping, as _CCR_FIELD_COLS does at src/ccreport/cache_db.py:1938):
- machines(machine_id PK, hostname, first_seen, last_seen)
- server_records: the ccreport_records columns plus machine_id, account_uuid, account_label, day and oslo_date computed at ingest, and cost NOT NULL because the client freezes it.
- ingest_files(machine_id, file_path, mtime_ns, size, n_records, updated_at) so a re-push of an unchanged file is a no-op and a re-push of a grown file replaces that file rows.
- Dedup on (account_uuid, dk) where dk is present, so a home directory synced between two machines does not double-count. Records with no dk fall back to (machine_id, file_path, ts, mid).

Configuration by environment variable, no config library: database path, bind address, port, and the shared token (the token itself belongs to the next issue).

Acceptance: just lint-all and just test pass; a test creates the schema in a tmp_path database and asserts the column tuple matches the CREATE TABLE, as tests/test_the_record_dict_matches_the_column_tuple does today.

Ingest endpoint and shared bearer token auth
description:
POST /v1/ingest accepting one machine batch: machine_id, hostname, ccreport client version, and a list of files, each with path, mtime_ns, size and its records. A record is the ccreport_records field set (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) plus account_uuid and account_label, with cost non-null.

Behaviour:
- Reject a batch whose Authorization header is not Bearer plus the configured shared token, with 401 and no detail. Auth is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33.
- A file whose (mtime_ns, size) already matches ingest_files is skipped and reported as skipped in the response, so the client can stop resending it.
- A file that changed replaces its rows in one transaction: delete by (machine_id, file_path), insert the batch. A JSONL only ever grows, but a rotated or truncated log must not leave stale rows.
- Respond with per-file accepted or skipped plus record counts, so the push client can update its local watermark from what the server actually stored rather than from what it hoped.
- Bound the request body size and return 413 above it. A full first push from a machine with 98k records must therefore be chunked by the client.

GET /v1/health returns version and record count without auth.

Acceptance: pytest tests using fastapi TestClient cover a good push, a wrong token, a re-push of an unchanged file, a re-push of a grown file, and an oversized body.

Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline
description:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), and cost frozen to what each record cost() answered. Chunk by record count so no request trips the server body limit.

Local state: a push_state table in cache.db keyed by (server_url, file_path) holding the (mtime_ns, size) the server acknowledged, plus a last_push_ts meta key per server URL. Never assume a push landed; write the watermark from the server response.

Machine identity: a uuid generated once and stored in the cache meta table, with the hostname sent alongside as a human label. Hostnames change and collide across networks; the uuid is what rows key on.

Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, at most one per 30 minutes, gated on a stored stamp the child writes on every outcome including failure, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). The status line must not import push.py: it spawns bin/ or python -m the same way it spawns usage_api.py. A render must never wait on the network.

Configuration: server URL and token from environment variables, absent means no push and no spawn, so a machine that has not opted in pays nothing.

Acceptance: tests cover the watermark skip, the changed-file resend, the chunking boundary, account stamping, and the 30-minute gate holding when the stamp is fresh. A statusline render with no server configured must spawn nothing; assert it.

Split report aggregation from rich rendering in ccreport.py
description:
Today the report commands in src/ccreport/ccreport.py both aggregate records and build rich tables in one pass. The server has to aggregate without rich, and the CLI has to render rows the server computed, so the two halves must separate before the read side can exist.

Work: for the day, month, project, session and account reports, extract a pure function that takes a record stream and returns rows as plain data, leaving the existing command to render those rows. No behaviour change and no output change on any existing report.

Watch the paths a report can take: a bare ccreport serves days older than ROLLUP_WINDOW_DAYS from ccreport_rollups while any filter, --json and adopt take the full record path (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). The extracted aggregation must be the one place both paths meet, or the server and the CLI will disagree on the same numbers.

Acceptance: existing tests pass untouched; new tests call the extracted functions directly and assert the row data; a golden test asserts the rendered output of each report is byte-identical to before the split.

Read side: ccreport --server renders the merged reports
description:
Server endpoints that aggregate, plus the CLI flag that renders them.

Server: GET /v1/report/{day,month,project,session,account} taking the same filters the CLI already offers, running the aggregation extracted by the refactor issue over server_records, and returning rows as JSON. Every response also breaks down by machine and by account, since that is the whole point of merging: one row set that says which machine and which account each number came from.

Client: ccreport --server URL <report> fetches those rows and renders them through the existing rich builders, so a merged report looks like a local one. Without --server, nothing about the local path changes.

Open points to settle while implementing:
- NOK conversion: exchange.py converts each record at its own Oslo-date rate. Decide whether the server converts (it needs the exchange_rates table and network) or returns USD and the client converts. Prefer server-side, so two clients cannot disagree.
- Project grouping: ccreport merge rules live in project_overrides on each client. Decide whether the server stores its own rules or the client sends resolved project names. Prefer resolving on the client at push time and treating the server name as final, so a merged report does not depend on which laptop asked.

Acceptance: tests spin the app with a seeded server database holding two machines and two accounts, and assert each report groups and totals correctly across both; a client test asserts rendering from a canned server response.

Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage
description:
A work laptop must push complete usage while revealing only the projects the user opted in to. Every record still goes to the server with its model, timestamps, token counts and cost. What a non-allowed record loses is identity: project, cwd and repo.

Configuration lives in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, not in cache.db, so a cache wipe cannot silently unredact a work machine:

  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport", "kantine"]
  salt = "<generated once on first run>"

restricted defaults to false. When the file is absent, the machine pushes everything with real names, which is what the two personal machines want. When restricted is true, a project not in allow is redacted. Fail closed: a malformed or unreadable push.toml on a machine that has ever been restricted must redact everything rather than fall back to open. Store the last known restricted state where the parser can see it before it trusts the file.

Names in allow are matched through the identity rules ccreport merge already applies, project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope() (AGENTS.md), so an alias resolves the same way a report groups it.

Redaction: project becomes a stable pseudonym, the first 8 hex of a hash over the salt and the resolved project name; cwd and repo become null. The salt never leaves the machine, so the server sees work-a1b2 as a durable grouping key it cannot reverse. Session ids of redacted records are hashed with the same salt, so sessions still group without carrying the original id.

Interaction with the push watermark: changing restricted or allow changes what past files should have sent. Store a hash of the effective policy alongside the watermark and force a full re-push when it changes, and have the server replace that machine rows rather than merge them, so a project moved from allow to redacted stops being named on the server.

Acceptance: tests cover an unrestricted machine sending real names, a restricted machine redacting a non-allowed project while its tokens and cost match the source records exactly, an allowed project surviving intact, the same project hashing to the same pseudonym across two runs, a malformed push.toml failing closed, and a policy change forcing a full re-push.

title: Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage
ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts
description:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups.
- Read surface: server-side CLI. ccreport renders tables the server computed. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one shared bearer token over HTTPS. The server binds a machine_id to the first client that used it and refuses a later push claiming it from a different client fingerprint, so a leaked token can add rows but cannot rewrite an existing machine history.
- Pricing: the server re-prices on ingest. Clients send token counts and the model id; the server computes cost with its own pricing.py, passing through only a cost the session log itself carried. One pricing source, so a machine that has not pulled cannot write wrong money into the merged history.
- Duplicates: every machine copy is stored. Reports collapse records by dedup key and attribute each to the machine that first reported it, so a synced home directory neither double-counts nor silently erases one machine contribution.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at most every 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push.
- Restricted machines: per-project opt-in with identity redaction, child issue ccreport-55s6.

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps account and machine onto each record before sending.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py, and it opens cache.db read-only, taking a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged.

Children: server package and schema, ingest endpoint and auth, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI, restricted-machine redaction.

title: ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts
Server package: FastAPI factory, Granian entry, merged SQLite schema
description:
Create src/ccreport/server/ holding the FastAPI app and its own SQLite database, separate from ~/.cache/ccreport/cache.db. The client cache stays a per-machine artifact; the server database is the merged one.

Follow ~/git/kantine: an app factory create_app() (src/km2/web/factory.py), a Granian entry point taking host/port/workers (src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py), and a justfile recipe. Add fastapi and granian with uv add, so uv.lock records them. Keep them out of the status line import path: statusline.py must still import stdlib only.

Schema, in a new module mirroring cache_db.py style (one column tuple driving SELECT, INSERT and row mapping, as _CCR_FIELD_COLS does at src/ccreport/cache_db.py:1938):
- machines(machine_id PK, hostname, client_fingerprint, first_seen, last_seen). client_fingerprint is recorded on the first push under that machine_id and is what a later push must match, since one shared token cannot tell two clients apart.
- server_records: the ccreport_records columns plus machine_id, account_uuid, account_label, day and oslo_date computed at ingest, and cost NOT NULL, computed by the server at ingest from pricing.py rather than taken from the client. Keep the client-sent log cost in its own column so a log-provided cost stays distinguishable from a computed one.
- ingest_files(machine_id, file_path, mtime_ns, size, n_records, updated_at) so a re-push of an unchanged file is a no-op and a re-push of a grown file replaces that file rows.
- No unique constraint on the dedup key: two machines pushing the same synced log both keep their rows. Index (account_uuid, dk) so read-time dedup can collapse them and attribute each record to the machine that first reported it.

Configuration by environment variable, no config library: database path, bind address, port, and the shared token (the token itself belongs to ccreport-23zb).

Acceptance: just lint-all and just test pass; a test creates the schema in a tmp_path database and asserts the column tuple matches the CREATE TABLE, as tests/test_the_record_dict_matches_the_column_tuple does today.

title: Server package: FastAPI factory, Granian entry, merged SQLite schema
Ingest endpoint and shared bearer token auth
description:
POST /v1/ingest accepting one machine batch: machine_id, hostname, client fingerprint, ccreport client version, and a list of files, each with path, mtime_ns, size and its records. A record is the ccreport_records field set (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) plus account_uuid and account_label. The client sends token counts and the model id; it sends a cost only when the session log itself carried one.

Behaviour:
- Reject a batch whose Authorization header is not Bearer plus the configured shared token, with 401 and no detail. Auth is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33.
- Price every record at ingest with the server pricing.py. A model id the server does not know must fail the file loudly and be reported in the response, never stored as zero: a silent zero is a week of money that looks like an idle week.
- Bind machine_id to the client fingerprint on first sight. A push claiming a known machine_id with a different fingerprint gets 409 and writes nothing, so one leaked token cannot rewrite another machine history.
- A file whose (mtime_ns, size) already matches ingest_files is skipped and reported as skipped, so the client can stop resending it.
- A file that changed replaces its rows in one transaction: delete by (machine_id, file_path), insert the batch. A JSONL only ever grows, but a rotated or truncated log must not leave stale rows. Deletes are scoped to the pushing machine and never touch another machine copy of the same synced log.
- Respond with per-file accepted, skipped or rejected plus record counts, so the push client updates its watermark from what the server stored rather than from what it hoped.
- Bound the request body size and return 413 above it. A full first push from a machine with 98k records must therefore be chunked by the client.

GET /v1/health returns version and record count without auth.

Acceptance: pytest tests using fastapi TestClient cover a good push, a wrong token, a fingerprint mismatch, an unknown model id, a re-push of an unchanged file, a re-push of a grown file, a second machine pushing the same log path, and an oversized body.

title: Ingest endpoint and shared bearer token auth
Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline
description:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9). Send token counts and the model id, and a cost only where the session log itself carried one: the server prices everything else, so no client can write wrong money into the merged history. Chunk by record count so no request trips the server body limit.

Cache access: open cache.db read-only, buffer what the batch needs, and take a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged. A render must never wait on this process, and a long-held lock on cache.db is what makes it wait.

Local state: a push_state table in cache.db keyed by (server_url, file_path) holding the acknowledged (mtime_ns, size), plus a last_push_ts meta key per server URL. Never assume a push landed; write the watermark from the server response, and leave a rejected file unrecorded so the next run retries it.

Machine identity: a uuid generated once and stored in the cache meta table, with the hostname sent alongside as a human label and a client fingerprint the server binds on first push. Hostnames change and collide across networks; the uuid is what rows key on.

Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent, skipped and had rejected.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, at most one per 30 minutes, gated on a stored stamp the child writes on every outcome including failure, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). The status line must not import push.py: it spawns the same way it spawns usage_api.py.

Configuration: server URL and token from environment variables. Absent means no push and no spawn, so a machine that has not opted in pays nothing.

Acceptance: tests cover the watermark skip, the changed-file resend, a rejected file being retried, the chunking boundary, account stamping, the read-only open, and the 30-minute gate holding when the stamp is fresh. A statusline render with no server configured must spawn nothing; assert it.

title: Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline
Split report aggregation from rich rendering in ccreport.py
description:
Today the report commands in src/ccreport/ccreport.py both aggregate records and build rich tables in one pass. The server has to aggregate without rich, and the CLI has to render rows the server computed, so the two halves must separate before the read side can exist.

Work: for the day, month, project, session and account reports, extract a pure function that takes a record stream and returns rows as plain data, leaving the existing command to render those rows. No behaviour change and no output change on any existing report.

Watch the paths a report can take: a bare ccreport serves days older than ROLLUP_WINDOW_DAYS from ccreport_rollups while any filter, --json and adopt take the full record path (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). The extracted aggregation must be the one place both paths meet, or the server and the CLI will disagree on the same numbers.

Acceptance:
- Existing tests pass untouched.
- New tests call the extracted functions directly and assert the row data.
- A golden test asserts the rendered output of each report is byte-identical to before the split.
- A parity test seeds one corpus that straddles ROLLUP_WINDOW_DAYS and asserts the rollup path and the full record path return identical rows. The golden fixtures alone can exercise one path only, which is exactly where a split like this diverges.

title: Split report aggregation from rich rendering in ccreport.py
Network gate: push only from an allowed CIDR
description:
A work laptop must only send stats while it is on the office network. The gate is evaluated before every push, manual and spawned alike, and a machine that fails it does nothing and records nothing.

Test: some local interface holds an address inside one of the configured CIDRs. Stdlib only, no packets, using socket and ipaddress so the statusline spawn stays cheap; do not probe the server to decide. A VPN that hands out an address in the range counts as being on the network, which is the intended behaviour.

Configuration in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, keyed per server URL alongside the restricted and allow keys from ccreport-55s6:

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  networks = ["10.172.0.0/22"]
  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport"]

An absent or empty networks list means no gate, which is what the personal machines want. A malformed CIDR must fail closed for that server, not be skipped: a typo in a work laptop config must never turn into pushing from a hotel wifi.

Interaction with the push watermark (ccreport-2r5m): a blocked push writes no watermark and no failure stamp beyond the 30-minute interval stamp, so everything queued simply goes out on the first run back inside the network. Nothing is lost by being off-network for a week.

ccreport push run by hand while off-network prints which server was skipped and which CIDRs it wanted, so the silence is explained rather than mysterious.

Acceptance: tests cover an interface inside the CIDR passing, every interface outside it blocking with no request sent, an absent networks key allowing the push, a malformed CIDR blocking, IPv6 handled or explicitly refused, and a queued file going out on the first allowed run.

title: Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage
ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts
description:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups. A request carries whole files only, never part of one, so every ingest transaction covers a complete file.
- Read surface: server-side CLI. ccreport renders tables the server computed. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one shared bearer token over HTTPS. The server binds a machine_id to the first client that used it and refuses a later push claiming it from a different client fingerprint, so a leaked token can add rows but cannot rewrite an existing machine history.
- Pricing: the server re-prices on ingest. Clients send token counts and the model id; the server computes cost with its own pricing.py, passing through only a cost the session log itself carried. One pricing source, so a machine that has not pulled cannot write wrong money into the merged history.
- Currency: the server converts, owning exchange.py and its own exchange_rates table, each record at its own Oslo-date rate. Two laptops asking the same question get the same number.
- Grouping: the client resolves the project name through its own ccreport merge rules before pushing, and the server treats the pushed name as final. A merged report does not depend on which laptop asked.
- Duplicates: every machine copy is stored. Reports collapse records by dedup key and attribute each to the machine that first reported it, so a synced home directory neither double-counts nor silently erases one machine contribution.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at most every 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push. The child writes an attempt stamp on every outcome and widens the interval on consecutive failures, so an unreachable server costs one process per interval rather than one per render.
- Restricted machines: per-project opt-in with identity redaction (ccreport-55s6) and a CIDR gate on pushing at all (ccreport-1ley).

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps account and machine onto each record before sending.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py, and it opens cache.db read-only, taking a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged.

Children: server package and schema, ingest endpoint and auth, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI, restricted-machine redaction, network gate.

title: ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts
Read side: ccreport --server renders the merged reports
description:
Server endpoints that aggregate, plus the CLI flag that renders them.

Server: GET /v1/report/{day,month,project,session,account} taking the same filters the CLI already offers, running the aggregation extracted by ccreport-3a79 over server_records, and returning rows as JSON. Every response also breaks down by machine and by account, since that is the whole point of merging: one row set that says which machine and which account each number came from.

Client: ccreport --server URL <report> fetches those rows and renders them through the existing rich builders, so a merged report looks like a local one. Without --server, nothing about the local path changes.

Two points settled with the user, no longer open:
- Currency: the server converts. It carries exchange.py and its own exchange_rates table and converts each record at its own Oslo-date rate, so two clients cannot disagree about the same week. A client asking for a report receives both USD and NOK.
- Project grouping: the client resolves the name through its own project_overrides before pushing (ccreport-2r5m) and the server treats it as final. The server holds no merge rules and never re-resolves.

Failure behaviour: an unreachable server prints what it tried and exits non-zero. Never fall back to the local cache silently, since a merged report and a single-machine report differ by exactly the thing being asked for.

Acceptance: tests spin the app with a seeded server database holding two machines and two accounts, and assert each report groups and totals correctly across both; a test asserts NOK conversion uses each record own Oslo date; a client test asserts rendering from a canned server response and a clear non-zero exit when the server is down.

title: Read side: ccreport --server renders the merged reports
Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline
description:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), and the project name already resolved through this machine project_overrides and pricing.project_scope(). The server treats that name as final and holds no merge rules of its own; a ccreport merge run therefore changes what past files should have sent, so fold the override rules into the policy hash that forces a full re-push in ccreport-55s6.

Send token counts and the model id, and a cost only where the session log itself carried one: the server prices everything else, so no client can write wrong money into the merged history.

Batching: a request carries whole files only, never part of one, so the server delete-then-insert for a file is always one transaction and a crashed push can never leave a committed delete with a partial re-insert. Pack as many whole files per request as the body limit allows. A single log too large for the limit is the one case needing a staged upload; treat it as a follow-up rather than the default path.

Cache access: open cache.db read-only, buffer what the batch needs, and take a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged. A render must never wait on this process, and a long-held lock on cache.db is what makes it wait.

Local state: a push_state table in cache.db keyed by (server_url, file_path) holding the acknowledged (mtime_ns, size), plus per-server meta keys for the last attempt and the consecutive failure count. Never assume a push landed; write the watermark from the server response, and leave a rejected file unrecorded so the next run retries it.

Machine identity: a uuid generated once and stored in the cache meta table, with the hostname sent alongside as a human label and a client fingerprint the server binds on first push. Hostnames change and collide across networks; the uuid is what rows key on.

Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent, skipped and had rejected.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, base interval 30 minutes. The child writes the attempt stamp on every outcome including failure and a blocked network gate, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules), and widens the interval on consecutive failures up to a cap, resetting to the base on the first success. A server down overnight must not be probed 20 times. The status line must not import push.py: it spawns the same way it spawns usage_api.py.

Configuration: server URL and token from environment variables. Absent means no push and no spawn, so a machine that has not opted in pays nothing.

Acceptance: tests cover the watermark skip, the changed-file resend, a rejected file being retried, whole-file batching at the body limit, account stamping, project resolution through an override rule, the read-only open, the attempt stamp written after a failure, the widened interval after consecutive failures and its reset on success. A statusline render with no server configured must spawn nothing; assert it.

title: Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline
Ingest endpoint and shared bearer token auth
description:
POST /v1/ingest accepting one machine batch: machine_id, hostname, client fingerprint, ccreport client version, and a list of files, each with path, mtime_ns, size and its records. A batch carries whole files only. A record is the ccreport_records field set (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) plus account_uuid and account_label, with the project name already resolved by the client. The client sends token counts and the model id; it sends a cost only when the session log itself carried one.

Behaviour:
- Reject a batch whose Authorization header is not Bearer plus the configured shared token, with 401 and no detail. Auth is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33.
- Price every record at ingest with the server pricing.py, and convert with the server exchange.py at each record own Oslo date. A model id the server does not know must fail the file loudly and be reported in the response, never stored as zero: a silent zero is a week of money that looks like an idle week.
- Bind machine_id to the client fingerprint on first sight. A push claiming a known machine_id with a different fingerprint gets 409 and writes nothing, so one leaked token cannot rewrite another machine history.
- A file whose (mtime_ns, size) already matches ingest_files is skipped and reported as skipped, so the client can stop resending it.
- A file that changed replaces its rows in one transaction: delete by (machine_id, file_path), insert the records that arrived in the same request. Because a request never carries part of a file, no crash can leave the delete committed without its re-insert. A JSONL only ever grows, but a rotated or truncated log must not leave stale rows. Deletes are scoped to the pushing machine and never touch another machine copy of the same synced log.
- Respond with per-file accepted, skipped or rejected plus record counts, so the push client updates its watermark from what the server stored rather than from what it hoped.
- Bound the request body size and return 413 above it, naming the limit in the response so a client with one oversized log can report it rather than retry forever.

GET /v1/health returns version and record count without auth.

Acceptance: pytest tests using fastapi TestClient cover a good push, a wrong token, a fingerprint mismatch, an unknown model id, a re-push of an unchanged file, a re-push of a grown file, a truncated file leaving no stale rows, a second machine pushing the same log path, and an oversized body.

- machines(machine_id PK, hostname, client_fingerprint, first_seen, last_seen). client_fingerprint is recorded on the first push under that machine_id and is what a later push must match, since one shared token cannot tell two clients apart.

title: Server package: FastAPI factory, Granian entry, merged SQLite schema
Web interface: machines and minted per-machine tokens
description:
A small server-rendered web interface whose one job is machine credentials: list machines, mint a token for a new one, revoke a token, rename a machine.

Pages:
- Machines: machine label, machine_id, last seen, record count, and whether its token is active or revoked. This is what answers the question the page will actually be opened for, which is whether that laptop is still reporting.
- Mint: name the machine, submit, and the new token is shown once. It is stored hashed, so it cannot be shown again; a lost token is re-minted, never recovered.
- Revoke: one action per token, effective immediately on the next push.

Access control: IP allowlist, no password. Allowed networks come from an environment variable, and the check is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33. The ingest endpoint keeps its own token auth and is NOT behind the allowlist: machines push from wherever they are. Anyone on an allowed network can mint, which is the accepted trade.

Tokens: 32 random bytes from secrets.token_urlsafe, stored as a hash with the machine_id it belongs to, created_at, last_used_at and revoked_at. Ingest looks a presented token up by hash and takes the machine_id from the row, so a machine can only ever write its own rows and the client fingerprint binding is unnecessary.

Rendering: server-rendered HTML with Jinja templates, the way ~/git/kantine does it. No JavaScript build step and no client framework for four pages of tables and two forms.

Acceptance: tests cover minting producing a token that ingest accepts, the token being unrecoverable from the database after minting, revocation causing 401 on the next push, a request from a disallowed address getting 403 on every UI route, and ingest still working from a disallowed address.
